   - that the **local engine's money cost is zero** and its latency was measured the same way, so it has a column like any other engine.

5. **The language result — a filter, not a score.** *(Guard block, run by you.)* **FACT:**
   - whether each engine recognised and spoke **Romanian**, and whether it is needed at all (the design's §4.7, D46's cell: language is "a hard filter, not a score" — a candidate without it is out);
   - which engines list Romanian at all, and that "automatic language detection" is a vendor's phrase and not a result — the register's §7 marks Deepgram's Romanian support **UNVERIFIED**.

6. **What the switch did, and what never went out.** *(Guard block, run by you; read-only.)* **FACT:**
   - that the indicator showed where each prompt went — **local**, **remote (<provider name>)**, or the checking state — and that a remote engine was reached **only** for a provider the project admitted and you had recorded consent for (§4.1, §4.3);
   - that the app **stored no audio** — no buffer, no spool, no retry queue, no file — and that any recording made to measure a latency stays **on the device, outside the repository and outside this switch** (§1a);
   - that the switch was back at **local** for the prompts that should not have gone anywhere, or that the badge said so if one did.

7. **The table, and the decision it feeds.** *(Guard block, run by you.)* **FACT:** the four numbers **side by side, one column per engine**, written down **before** your own impression is — the design's point is an impression **with numbers beside it**, so the numbers are the record and the impression is commentary on it. **FACT:** that this table is what Voice D44's second egress decision and the choice among the three providers are taken against, and that this check **takes neither**.

**Passes when:** the **local engine** and **every provider the project admits** each has all four numbers — first partial, end-of-speech-to-reply, name error rate and cost per hour — recorded against the **oldest device** and the **same written-down prompt list**, each rate against **its own denominator**; the cost per hour carries the price source it was computed from and the date that price was read; the language result is recorded as the filter it is; and the indicator's state matched the engine each prompt actually reached.

**Fails when:** a number is recorded for an engine that was never put the prompts through; a latency, a rate or a cost is stated without its denominator, its device or its conditions; the **local** engine's absence is papered over by measuring a remote engine and calling it the local one; two engines were measured under different prompts or different conditions; a page's **list price** is quoted as the **measured** rate; a rate or a cost is inferred, averaged or guessed rather than read from the pass; audio is recorded off the device and kept; or the prompt list is changed after the first utterance so the denominators move.

**Paste back:** the device and its OS, the app's build and version, the engines measured and the `config/policy/voice` node they came from; the fixed prompt list; for each engine the four numbers — first partial, end-of-speech-to-reply, the name error rate with both counts, and cost per hour with its price source and the date read; the language result per engine; and the indicator's state per prompt. **The recordings themselves are never pasted**, and **no credential, ID token, MAC key or provider key is read by this check or appears in any `FACT` line.**

**Restore.** Nothing to undo: this check writes no node, mints no token, makes no commit and changes no setting — set the two switch settings back to **local** when you are done, which is the default the design starts from (§4.1). The app's install is check 89's and the phone's paired device is check 100's; any recording made to measure a latency is yours to delete from the device. No provider audio is stored by the app at any step, and the mailbox still carries text.

## Check 86: hands-free audio — the background mode, the microphone ask, Bluetooth, and barge-in (your own phone, a real headset, and the app check 89 built; run by you; NOT RUN)

**NOT RUN.** This check is **Task P4.2**'s, written against the register's own row **86** — *"Hands-free audio: the background mode, the microphone ask, Bluetooth, and barge-in"*, attributed to Tasks **P3.5** and **P4.2**, and whose own "why it cannot be a test" is the stub *"Needs a real device and a real headset"* — and **no agent runs any step of it**: its whole subject is what a real OS does with a real microphone through a real headset. It is the live half of the mobile reconciliation's **U7** — *whether the OS grants background audio with barge-in on both platforms* — which no device has answered (`docs/mobile/reconciliation.md`, the U7 row sends it here), and it is the measurement the voice-session work's **U3** names (*whether `AudioManager.MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION` makes the platform apply echo cancellation*, `docs/mobile/voice-session/reconciliation.md`, U3).

**Why it is not a test, and the one reading it takes.** Global Constraint 10 keeps a device, a microphone and a live OS out of CI — the pure logic is already proven over the fakes (`mobile/src/audio/pipeline.test.js`, `mobile/src/voice/screen.test.js`, `mobile/src/voice/interrupt.test.js`, `mobile/src/voice-session/machine.test.js`) and none of that is what this check is for. **Check 86 is written to run with the session up and the pipeline silent**, which is the voice-session work's **D208** — *"every check is written to run with the session up and the pipeline silent … the one thing that must wait for Check 85 is the 'I'm back' cue and anything that depends on real speech"* — and that is the reading taken here: the app is **voiceless** today (no STT/TTS engine is declared in `mobile/package.json`, check 85's bake-off is unrun; the pipeline's ports on a phone are P3.4's fakes, and nothing in `mobile/index.js` starts the session). So the background mode, the microphone ask and the Bluetooth route are all observable with **nothing said**, and the one part of **barge-in** that depends on real speech — the assistant audibly cut off by the owner's own voice, and the AEC **U3** measures — **waits for Check 85** rather than being faked here.

**Why a live check, when the fakes are tested.** The voice-session reconciliation's own device table is the answer, and it is per half: *"The mic ask, the background mode, the indicator"* is **Required / Required / Partly — "the permission dialog can be answered, but the *background* behaviour is not the same"**, and *"Unplugging a headset / dropping Bluetooth mid-response"* is **Required / Required / No**, because *"`ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` is documented as a **hint** (P18), and no emulator produces a real route change"* (`docs/mobile/voice-session/reconciliation.md`, its device table). A fake proves the screen's rule over a route event; only a phone and a headset prove the OS **emits** the route event and that the mic **survives** a lock screen — which is the whole of **U7** and the half of **U3** a desk cannot answer.

**The two platforms, and the two halves of U7.** The check is run on each platform you own, because the reconciliation's evidence differs per platform and the two answers are different facts:

- **iOS.** The background mode is `UIBackgroundModes: audio` — *"To continue playing audio when your app transitions to the background (for example, when the screen locks), add the `audio` value"* (reconciliation P6, Apple's `AVAudioSession.Category.playAndRecord`) — and the spec's `.voiceChat` mode is **wrong as written** about AEC: the mode reduces the allowed routes and applies `allowBluetoothHFP`, and echo cancellation is the Voice I/O audio unit's, not the mode's (reconciliation P7). The route signal is `RouteChangeReason.oldDeviceUnavailable`, posted on a **secondary** thread (reconciliation P9).
- **Android.** A backgrounded session needs the microphone foreground service — `foregroundServiceType="microphone"`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE` and the runtime `RECORD_AUDIO` prerequisite (reconciliation P12) — and it **cannot be started from the background**: *"you cannot create a microphone foreground service while your app is in the background"*, so the session starts while the app is in the foreground (P11). The route signal is the **hint** `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` (P18), and `MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION` is **not** what applies AEC — that is the separate, device-dependent `AcousticEchoCanceler` (P20, U3).

**The four subjects, and who owns them.** `docs/mobile/voice-session/reconciliation.md` **F17** is the boundary: the voice-session work does **not** rewrite Check 86 and does **not** claim it — 86 *"keeps its number and its subject"*, and where the two touch (*"the Bluetooth route, and the microphone ask"*) **86 keeps them**. **D122** is the ruling under three of the four: the microphone is an OS permission with a usage-description string **the owner writes**, Bluetooth input goes through the platform's audio route, and the app **degrades to a visible "tap to speak" control** when the OS refuses background audio or the microphone; **D207** extends D122 so that the background audio mode is declared for the session's whole existence and not only for barge-in (F2's reversal of the console's "no background listening").

**What this check does not cover (F17's other half).** F17's list of what 86 does **not** name is the voice-session work's, so those run **once**, in the checks **113–118** the voice-session plan's **D219** takes: *"a call arriving mid-session, an unplug **mid-response**, the Live Activity's buttons, the Android notification's actions, and what a force-kill leaves behind"*. This check records the **route change itself** and the **pause** it produces, and hands the **unplug mid-response** — the assistant audibly cut off by the headset leaving — to the voice-session checks (113–118). It also re-runs none of the mailbox checks: **check 100** pairs a phone, and 86 pairs nothing and writes nothing.

**What the committed config carries today (read from the files, not assumed).** `mobile/app.json`'s `expo.ios` is `{ "supportsTablet": false }` and its `expo.android` carries only `adaptiveIcon`; `mobile/app.config.js` adds the export-compliance plist key (`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption: false`), the Firebase plugin entries, the two identity fields resolved from `FUGARO_IOS_BUNDLE_ID`/`FUGARO_ANDROID_PACKAGE`, and `android.blockedPermissions` (the advertising-id removal). **Neither file carries `UIBackgroundModes`, `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`, or any Android permission** — the declarations are **VS2**'s (`docs/mobile/voice-session/implementation-plan.md`, VS2.1 the iOS four, VS2.2 the Android four, marked *"still owed"*; D207 gates VS2.1), which is **why the guard below stops today**.

**Guard block — re-run this before every step.** It stops unless the checkout carries the voice screen, the audio pipeline and the session this check drives — and unless the config declares the background audio mode and the microphone ask, which it does not.

```bash
# === Check 86: setup + guard. RE-RUN THIS BLOCK BEFORE EVERY STEP. ===
set -u
ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || { echo "Check 86 stopped: not inside a git checkout; this check runs against a build of the app in this repository" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -d "$ROOT/mobile/src/voice" ] || { echo "Check 86 stopped: there is no mobile/src/voice/ in this checkout, so the screen this check drives (P3.5: the interrupt switch, the offline refusal, the lease) is not on this tree" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -d "$ROOT/mobile/src/audio" ] || { echo "Check 86 stopped: there is no mobile/src/audio/ in this checkout, so the pipeline whose barge-in this check measures (P3.4: audio-in, stt, tts) is not on this tree" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -d "$ROOT/mobile/src/voice-session" ] || { echo "Check 86 stopped: there is no mobile/src/voice-session/ in this checkout, so there is no session to background, interrupt or route (voice-session VS1; the Bluetooth half is here)" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -f "$ROOT/mobile/eas.json" ] || { echo "Check 86 stopped: there is no mobile/eas.json in this checkout, so there is no build for the phone to install — check 89 is where the app is built, and this check starts where that one ends" >&2; exit 1; }
grep -q 'UIBackgroundModes' "$ROOT/mobile/app.config.js" "$ROOT/mobile/app.json" 2>/dev/null || { echo "Check 86 stopped: neither mobile/app.json nor mobile/app.config.js declares UIBackgroundModes, so the background audio mode this check is about is not in the tree — the declaration is VS2.1's (voice-session plan), gated on D207, and not built" >&2; exit 1; }
grep -q 'NSMicrophoneUsageDescription' "$ROOT/mobile/app.config.js" "$ROOT/mobile/app.json" 2>/dev/null || { echo "Check 86 stopped: neither file declares NSMicrophoneUsageDescription, so the microphone ask this check is about has no usage string for the OS to show (D122: the string is the owner's; VS2.1 lands the key)" >&2; exit 1; }
grep -q 'RECORD_AUDIO' "$ROOT/mobile/app.config.js" 2>/dev/null || { echo "Check 86 stopped: mobile/app.config.js declares no android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO, so the Android microphone ask and the foreground-service type this check is about are not in the manifest (VS2.2)" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "Check 86 ready: the session is up and the pipeline is silent by design (D208) — with the declarations in the tree and the phone installed from check 89's build, nothing spoken is required, and no credential is read or pasted"
```

**What you need to have, before step 1.** Nothing this check buys or builds — it creates no cloud resource, launches no run and writes no node — but four things, and the guard above is what says they are in the tree before you start:

- **The build check 89 produced, installed on the phone**: its `internal` profile reaches TestFlight and the Play internal track, and a `development`/`preview` build installs the same way (`mobile/README.md`, "Building for internal testing"). This check starts where that one ends.
- **A real Bluetooth headset**, and a **wired** one if you have it — the route check is worth running on both, because the platform signals differ.
- **Your phone's own Settings**, to grant and revoke the microphone — step 3 is the permission being taken away, and no app control can do that.
- **Both platforms, if you own both**: **U7** asks the question of iOS *and* Android, and one answer is one platform's.

1. **The install, and the ask.** *(Guard block, run by you, at your terminal and on the phone.)* Start a session from the app's own control. Record the OS microphone dialog **as it appeared** — the sentence is the owner's `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` — and **grant** it. **FACT:** the device and its OS, the app's build and version, the permission string exactly as the dialog showed it, the grant, and the app's own state once the session is up (`mobile/src/voice/screen.js`'s `state()` — `microphone` `{ ok: true }`, `switch` `off` by D127). **Nothing is said, and nothing needs to be.**

2. **The background mode — U7's first half.** *(Guard block, run by you, on the phone.)* With the session up, press home and lock the screen, and leave it a minute. **FACT:** whether the session **survives** the app being backgrounded and the screen locked — the in-app indicator or the OS's own "recording" mark still there, and on return the session still up rather than torn down. Read it per platform, because the two facts are different:

   - **iOS:** *"the iOS orange dot / the app's own indicator is still present while the app is not on screen"* — the mic is suspended without `UIBackgroundModes: audio` (spec §6.6, reconciliation P6), so its presence is the mode working.
   - **Android:** *"the status-bar icon (and the session's own notification) is still there, and the service was not killed"* — a backgrounded session needs the microphone foreground service (§7.1, reconciliation P12), and Android 14 refuses to **start** one from the background (P11), so it must have started while the app was in the foreground.

   **FACT:** *"the mic stayed alive while the app was not on screen"* is **U7**'s answer for that platform.

3. **The ask, refused — D122's degradation.** *(Guard block, run by you, on the phone.)* Revoke the microphone permission in the OS settings (or answer **Don't allow** on a fresh install) and start the session again; then, on a second device or install if you have one, exercise the **background-audio-denied** path. **FACT:** the app shows the visible **"tap to speak"** control and does **not** pretend to listen — the screen's `microphone` carries one of D122's two codes (`mobile/src/audio/audio-in.js`, `AUDIO_IN_CODES`), and the `unavailable` event carried that code (`mobile/src/audio/pipeline.js`, `PIPELINE_EVENTS`). **FACT:** which code each refusal produced — `microphone-denied` or `background-audio-denied`, the two and no third — and that a denied session is one a control is built on rather than a silent one (D122, D215).

4. **Bluetooth — the route.** *(Guard block, run by you, on the phone, with your own headset.)* Pair a real Bluetooth headset (and, if you have one, a wired one), start the session, and read the route it reports (`mobile/src/voice-session/events.js`, `AUDIO_ROUTES`: `speaker`, `receiver`, `wired`, `bluetooth`, `usb`, `unknown`) and the `routeChanged { route, unsafe }` events it emits. **FACT:** three transitions — the route before the headset connects, the route while it is connected, and the change when it **disconnects mid-session**, which must arrive as `routeChanged { unsafe: true }` (spec §6.3/§7.5, `SESSION_STATES`' `paused_route`) with the session **paused** and **not** continuing through the loudspeaker, and a **reconnect**, which must arrive as `unsafe: false` and continue on the new route (spec §6.4). **FACT:** the platform's own signal behind it — iOS's `RouteChangeReason.oldDeviceUnavailable` and Android's `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` — recorded as: did the app pause, or did the owner hear the reply switch to the phone's own speaker? **The unplug mid-response** (the assistant audibly cut off) is **not** this step's; it is the voice-session checks' (F17, D219's 113–118).

5. **Barge-in — the boundary, and the half that waits.** *(Guard block, run by you, on the phone; read-only.)* With the session up and the pipeline **silent**, drive the turn the fakes make observable: an utterance in flight, and a capture event (`barge-in`, or a plain `speech-start`, `mobile/src/audio/audio-in.js`) arriving during it. **FACT:** the utterance reports itself **interrupted** and the boundary frees (`mobile/src/audio/pipeline.js`, `PIPELINE_EVENTS`' `utterance` with `state: 'interrupted'`), with nothing said. **FACT that is a deferral, not a result:** the genuinely **spoken** barge-in — the assistant audible through the headset and the owner's voice cutting it off — and the echo cancellation **U3** names need a real engine and real speech, so they **are not run here** and **wait for Check 85**. Record that they were skipped, not that they passed.

**Passes when:** step 1 records the dialog's own string, the grant and the session's state; step 2 shows the session (and the OS's recording mark) surviving the app being backgrounded and the screen locked, on each platform you own — which is **U7**; step 3 shows both denial codes driving the visible fallback rather than a silent session; step 4 shows the route the session reports for a real headset, `unsafe: true` on a mid-session disconnect with the session **paused** and never the loudspeaker, and `unsafe: false` on reconnect; and step 5's boundary reports **interrupted**, with the spoken half and **U3** recorded as skipped and waiting for Check 85.

**Fails when:** the dialog's sentence is not the owner's, or the permission asks for more than the app uses; a denied permission leaves the app **listening** or claiming to; the session dies when the app is backgrounded or the screen is locked with the mode declared (U7 answered no on that platform); a disconnected headset sends the reply to the loudspeaker (`unsafe` not raised, or the session not paused); a reconnect does not continue on the new route; or a step's **FACT** reports the spoken barge-in or an AEC result **without** Check 85 having been run — the one claim this check must not make.

**Paste back:** the device and its OS, the app's build and version (check 89's), the dialog's string and the answer, the app's own state on each denial, the route and each `routeChanged`'s `unsafe` flag with what the owner heard, and the boundary's outcome. **No credential, token, MAC key or recording is pasted** — the permission string is the owner's public sentence, and the recordings stay on the device.

**Restore.** Nothing written by hand and nothing to undo: no node, no token, no run, no commit.

- The only setting this check changes is the phone's own microphone permission; grant it again (or leave it refused) as you wish — the app's fallback is designed either way.
- The app's install is **check 89**'s and any paired device is **check 100**'s; this check pairs nothing and writes nothing.
- The recordings the pass produced (if any) are yours to delete from the device; they are never pasted.

## Check 87: multi-account switching with no cross-leakage — two real installations on one phone, one of them `belong` (installation `fugaro` and `belong`, your own phone, at your own terminal; run by you; NOT RUN)

**NOT RUN.** Task P4.2 writes this check and running it is the owner's; the row is a later addition to the 80–89 block (**added by hand**), and the register's own allocation
paragraph names **80 and 83–88** as Task **P4.2**'s — written by it into this file on 2026-11-17 — and counts the seven there. Its subject is **D114** — an account *is* an installation (one Firebase project, one Auth
`uid`, one Fugaro project name), several held as **separate, non-overlapping** entries with a switcher that **tears down the previous account's listeners and caches before it opens
the next** — and **D126**, which names the **multi-account isolation rule** as one of the pure functions tested against fakes with no runtime and no network. **`belong` is the owner's
own installation, added by hand, and no agent touches it** (F31, Global Constraint 11); this check names it as one of the two, and its guard refuses an agent's session and refuses
until you type the owner gate.

**This is the phone's installation switcher, and it is not `fugaro accounts switch`.** The subject lives in `mobile/src/accounts/` (the store: `account.js`, `secure-store.js`,
`secret.js`, `resources.js`, `store.js`) and `mobile/src/overview/` (P6.8's switcher, tiles and screen). `fugaro accounts switch FROM TO` is a different command entirely — it moves a
machine's **model-account** keys (`default_claude_account`, `stages.*.claude_account`, `crafts.*.access`, `repos.*.claude_accounts`, `profiles.*.claude_accounts`) in the local project
config (`internal/cli/accounts_switch.go`, `internal/localcfg`) and touches **no phone**; nothing here exercises it.

**Why it is a live check when the store is tested.** The isolation is a pure function and the tests already prove it — `mobile/src/accounts/store.test.js`'s *"switching closes the
previous account before it opens the next"*, *"two configured accounts never answer with each other's values"*, *"a switch closes every account open in the registry, not only the one
it recorded"* — over the fakes D126 names. What no test can see is a **phone** holding two **real** installations, signed in to two real Firebase projects, switching while a real
mailbox is read and a real reply is spoken: that is what only the device shows, and it is the negative this check exists for.

**What a leak would look like, surface by surface.** The phone has five surfaces an installation's data can reach, and each is named here so a leak is a fact and not a feeling:
the **shell** (`mobile/src/app/root.js` shows the current account's id and nothing else); the **tiles** (`mobile/src/overview/tiles.js` — one per installation, its own `spend`,
`dailyCap`, `percent`, `runs` and freshness, and **no summed total**, so a figure of A on B's tile must be impossible); the **feed** (`mobile/src/feed/paths.js`'s `FAMILIES`:
`config/caps`, `config/kill`, `spend`, `mailbox`); the **mailbox** (`mobile/src/mailbox/paths.js` — the phone's own `inbox` write, its `outbox` read and the `acked` child); and the
**spoken reply** (`mobile/src/voice/screen.js`, spoken from an outbox message the phone verified). There is **no push notification to test** — D121 keeps v1 without it — so "a
notification" here is the feed, a tile and the spoken proactive update, and A's must all be gone.

**Guard block — re-run this before every step.** It refuses an agent's session (this check names `belong`), it refuses until you type the owner gate, and **it stops today**: the
app's entry wires no pairing/overview screen, so no installation can be added on the phone.

```bash
# === Check 87: setup + guard. RE-RUN THIS BLOCK BEFORE EVERY STEP. ===
set -u
ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || { echo "Check 87 stopped: not inside a git checkout; the app this check drives is built from mobile/ in this repository" >&2; exit 1; }
env | grep -Eq '^(CLAUDECODE|CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT|CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE|CURSOR_AGENT|AI_AGENT)=' && { echo "Check 87 stopped: a coding agent's marker is set in this shell; this check switches between two installations, one of them belong, and no agent touches belong (F31) — run it yourself at your own terminal. The five read here are internal/agentenv's AgentMarkers, the ones an agent sets whatever the terminal; CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT is deliberately not among them, because the IDE extension sets it in a person's own integrated terminal too" >&2; exit 1; }
[ "${CHK87_OWNER_RUN:-}" = yes ] || { echo "Check 87 stopped: type CHK87_OWNER_RUN=yes at your own terminal before this check reads anything; it names belong, the owner's own installation, and every step of it is yours" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -d "$ROOT/mobile/src/accounts" ] || { echo "Check 87 stopped: there is no mobile/src/accounts/ in this checkout, so the account store whose isolation this check proves is not here (P3.1)" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -d "$ROOT/mobile/src/overview" ] || { echo "Check 87 stopped: there is no mobile/src/overview/ in this checkout, so there is no switcher to switch with (P6.8)" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -f "$ROOT/internal/cli/pair.go" ] || { echo "Check 87 stopped: there is no internal/cli/pair.go in this checkout, so an installation cannot be paired on the phone and there are no two accounts to switch between (P6.6)" >&2; exit 1; }
grep -q 'pairingScreen: null' "$ROOT/mobile/index.js" && { echo "Check 87 stopped: mobile/index.js wires no pairing/overview screen (it passes pairingScreen: null), so no installation can be added on the phone and two live accounts cannot exist — P6.8's createOverview is built and mobile/src/overview/index.js says nothing wires it yet" >&2; exit 1; }
grep -q 'mailbox-not-wired' "$ROOT/mobile/index.js" && { echo "Check 87 stopped: the app's client is a wiring stand-in (unpairedClient, whose every call answers mailbox-not-wired), so the phone reads and writes no real mailbox and a leak would have nothing to show up in" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "Check 87 ready: two real installations you added by hand, one of them belong, on your own phone — the ID token and the MAC key are never printed or pasted, and no agent runs any step of this"
```

1. **The two installations, and what identifies each.** *(Guard block, run by you.)* Add both installations to the phone **by hand** (D114: the list is the owner's, typed, never a
   discovery result) — `fugaro` and `belong` — each paired through `fugaro pair` (`internal/cli/pair.go`), which mints a **device token** and writes the **device node**
   `config/admin/devices/<uid>`.
   - **FACT:** for each, the account **id** (the label you typed — `mobile/src/accounts/account.js`'s alphabet), its **Firebase project id**, its **Auth `uid`** (the mailbox id the
     rules bind: `$mb == auth.uid`), and its **Fugaro project name**.
   - **FACT:** the two tuples differ in **all three** of the last three fields — a second entry for one installation is refused (`DUPLICATE_INSTALLATION`), so "two accounts" is
     two installations and not one under two labels.
   - **FACT:** each account holds exactly D111's two items (`SECRET_ITEMS = ['idToken', 'macKey']`, `mobile/src/accounts/secret.js`), in platform **secure storage** and not in a
     settings file (`mobile/src/accounts/settings.js`'s fences).

2. **Open A, and take a reading of everything on the phone.** *(Guard block, run by you, on the phone.)* Switch to installation **A** — spoken "Fugaro, switch to <A>" (the router
   requires the wake word; the switcher resolves the spoken name against `store.list()` and refuses an unconfigured one with `NO_SUCH_ACCOUNT`), or the overview's own switcher.
   - **FACT:** the shell shows **A's id** as the current account and nothing else (`mobile/src/app/root.js`); A's **tile** carries A's own `spend`, `dailyCap`, `percent`, `runs` and
     freshness (`liveness`, `ageMs`, `silenceMs`).
   - **FACT:** the feed reads A's own nodes — `config/caps/**`, `config/kill/**`, `spend/$day/**`, and `mailbox/<A's uid>/{outbox,heartbeat}` — and a read of a node the grant does
     not cover is never requested.
   - **FACT:** a message you have A speak is written to `mailbox/<A's uid>/inbox/$msg` with `sender` **A's uid**, and A's per-account **MAC key** (`mobile/src/mailbox/mac.js`, the
     direction inside the covered bytes) is the key A's replies verify under.

3. **Switch to B, and prove that not one thing of A survives.** *(Guard block, run by you, on the phone.)* Speak "Fugaro, switch to <B>". The store **closes A first and opens B
   second** (`store.switchTo`), closing **every** account the registry holds open. **This is the check's core, and every line below is a leak if it fails:**
   - **FACT:** after the switch the shell shows **B's id**; the feed's read paths name **B's uid**, never `mailbox/<A's uid>/…`; B's tile carries **B's** figures and freshness and
     none of A's; and A's spend, cap, runs and heartbeat appear **nowhere** on B's screen — a figure of A already drawn is **gone**, not stale-but-visible.
   - **FACT:** a reply A's consumer wrote to `mailbox/<A's uid>/outbox` is **not spoken** while B is open; if it reaches B at all it **fails B's key** (`verifyMac` false — a tag made
     for A's key and A's direction does not verify under B's), so the phone **drops it rather than speaking it**.
   - **FACT:** an ack is written only after the phone has spoken a message, and it lands on the **open** account's own `outbox/$msg/acked` — never the other's.
   - **FACT:** no listener from A is alive — the observable is that **no value arrives from A** (no sender A, no A heartbeat, no A figure) after the switch, which is `store.switchTo`'s
     tested teardown made live.

4. **Switch back to A, and prove the reverse.** *(Guard block, run by you, on the phone.)* Speak "Fugaro, switch to <A>" again.
   - **FACT:** B's data does not appear under A — B's uid in any `mailbox/…` path, B's heartbeat, B's figures, B's `sender`; the shell shows A's id; and nothing B was showing survives.
   - **FACT:** the switch **back** is the same as forward: there is no moment with two installations live (a teardown that failed leaves **no** current account rather than open the
     next — `TEARDOWN_FAILED`), and a spoken switch to an unconfigured name is refused **before** anything is opened or closed.

5. **The fence across the two installations, and what the check did not touch.** *(Guard block, read-only.)*
   - **FACT:** the two installations are **two Firebase projects**, **two Auth uids** and **two device nodes** (`config/admin/devices/<uid>`), and a read of A's mailbox with B's
     credentials is **denied by the rules** — `MAILBOX` is `userClaim && $mb == auth.uid`, so B's token reaches only `mailbox/<B's uid>` whatever the phone does. The database, not
     the app, is the fence that holds **across** installations; the phone's own teardown is what holds **within** one.
   - **FACT:** `belong` was touched by **no agent**, was not written by this check beyond the phone's own account and read, and **no ID token, device token or MAC key was read, printed
     or pasted** by any step.

**Passes when:** step 1's two installations carry two distinct tuples and exactly D111's two items live in secure storage; step 2's reading ties A's figures, freshness, mailbox paths
and `sender` to A's own uid; step 3 shows **B's** screen holding none of A — no A read, no A write, no A figure, no A feed item, no A reply spoken, and the reply that fails B's key
dropped rather than spoken; step 4 shows the reverse clean and the store never two-live; and step 5's fence is the rules', with no credential read or pasted anywhere.

**Fails when:** after a switch, **any** value of the account left behind shows under the one now open — a figure on the wrong tile, a heartbeat of A rendered as B's, A's uid in a
`mailbox/…` read path, a message with A's `sender` spoken while B is current, or an A feed item that stays on screen; a listener of the old account is still alive (a value arrives
from A after the switch); a write lands in the **other** account's `inbox` or acks the other's outbox; the switch opens the next account before the previous teardown has run (two
installations live at once); `config/admin/devices` is read by a client token; or a token or a MAC key is echoed to a terminal, a log, a settings file or a `FACT` line — the fix is on
the phone or in the store, never in this document.

**Paste back:** the two account **ids** (the labels you typed, not secrets), the two Firebase project ids, the two Auth uids and the two Fugaro project names; the phone and its OS and
the app's build; A's reading and B's reading from steps 2–3 and what each screen held after each switch; whether any value arrived from the account left behind, and the reply that
failed the wrong key if you tried it; and that `belong` was untouched by any agent. **Never paste an ID token, a device token, a MAC key or a private key**, and nothing here is a
credential.

**Restore.** Nothing to undo on either installation: this check writes no node by hand, mints no token, makes no commit and changes no setting beyond the two accounts the phone itself
holds — a switch and a read, and the phone's own inbox message if you sent one.

- The two accounts **stay**: a phone holding two installations is the point of the check, and removing one is `fugaro pair revoke` (check 101) or removing the app, not this check.
- The phone's two items stay in secure storage; no key was written to a file by this check, so there is nothing to delete on your machine.
- **`belong` is left exactly as it was** — the owner's own installation, added by hand, never touched by an agent, and nothing in `belong` was created, changed, read or deleted by this
  check beyond the phone's own account.

## Check 88: a push per category, a payload carrying a category and nothing else, a revoke that ends delivery for good, and a lure the app must not act on (installation `fugaro`, your own phone and a real push service, never `belong`; run by you; NOT RUN)

**NOT RUN.** Task **P4.2** writes this check — the mobile plan allocates the writing to it ("checks 80 and 
83–88 by P4.2", Task **P4.2: Checks 80–89, written into the register") — and **running it is the 
owner's**. Its subject is the push design's own outline: `docs/mobile/design/push-notifications.md` **§8**, 
"What Check 88 would have to prove". **D121 was answered "no push in v1" on 2026-10-17** 
(`docs/mobile/reconciliation.md`, D121: push is "a separate decision with its own service, its own 
device-token store and its own retention question"); **the owner gave that later yes on 2026-11-14**, 
approving **P5.2** and splitting it into **P5.2.1–P5.2.10**. So the design is of record and the number is 
held — **but this check is run by the owner only if the owner builds push**, and the check drives things 
that are **not built**: the app's registration and its receipt are **P5.2.8** and **P5.2.9** 
(`mobile/src/push/`, absent), and the account that may send is **P5.2.7** (a Terraform grant that exists 
nowhere). The sender that derives the events and calls FCM is **P5.2.6**, and it IS built 
(`internal/cli/push.go`, merged: the sweep derives its own events, holds the ledger, the cap, the dedupe 
and the quiet hours, and calls FCM), so the guard below stops on the app and on the grant and not on the 
sender. **No agent performs any step of it**, and nothing on it touches `belong`.

**Why a live check, and what a unit test cannot see.** The rules cases (P5.2.2 and P5.2.3, merged: 
`internal/budget/rules/rules_test.go` and its `firebase`-tagged `emulator_push_test.go`) prove that **no 
client token** may read or write `config/admin/push/$uid`, and the schema's own cases prove the app's write 
path refuses an unknown field. They cannot prove the three things this check is for: that a **real** push 
reaches a **real** phone for each category; that the payload **as FCM and APNs store it** carries a category 
and nothing else; and — the step that matters most — that a **hand-crafted lure** in a title, sent 
through the installation's **own** FCM project, makes the app open and show the truth and **never act**, 
never render the lure as state and never as a link (design §8; §4 rules 3, 8 and 11; §3.9; §5 attacker 2; 
Q6 — under the recommended **(i)** the payload carries **no id**, so the alert is posted only on a **new, 
MAC-verified** mailbox change).

**Guard block — re-run this before every step.** It stops unless the checkout carries the sender, the app's 
push library and registration, the FCM grant and the registration path. **It stops today**, and each refusal 
names the task that would build the missing thing.

```bash
# === Check 88: setup + guard. RE-RUN THIS BLOCK BEFORE EVERY STEP. ===
set -u
ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || { echo "Check 88 stopped: not inside a git checkout; the sender, the app and the rules this check drives are all read out of this repository" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -f "$ROOT/internal/cli/push.go" ] || { echo "Check 88 stopped: there is no internal/cli/push.go in this checkout, so the sender that derives its own events, holds the ledger, the cap, the dedupe and the quiet hours, and calls FCM is not built (P5.2.6, the sender, level 7) — nothing buzzes a phone, so no step below can observe anything" >&2; exit 1; }
grep -q '"@react-native-firebase/messaging"\|"expo-notifications"' "$ROOT/mobile/package.json" || { echo "Check 88 stopped: mobile/package.json declares no push library (no FCM/APNs messaging, no Expo push), so the app neither registers for a push nor receives one (P5.2.8)" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -d "$ROOT/mobile/src/push" ] || { echo "Check 88 stopped: there is no mobile/src/push/ in this checkout, so the app's registration and the receipt that must not act do not exist (P5.2.8 registers, P5.2.9 is the receipt: the alert, and no action, no route, no write)" >&2; exit 1; }
grep -rq 'firebasecloudmessaging.messages.create' "$ROOT/deploy/terraform/gcp/modules" || { echo "Check 88 stopped: no Terraform module grants firebasecloudmessaging.messages.create, so no account may send a push (P5.2.7). The permission is listed in deploy/terraform/testdata/custom-role-permissions.txt, a catalogue and not a grant, and the FCM API (firebasecloudmessaging.googleapis.com) is enabled by no apis.tf" >&2; exit 1; }
grep -q 'config/admin/push' "$ROOT/internal/cli/mailbox.go" || { echo "Check 88 stopped: internal/cli/mailbox.go does not apply a registration to config/admin/push/\$uid, so nothing writes the push node the sender reads (P5.2.4) — today fugaro pair revoke only DELETES that node (P5.2.5, merged, #2863) and no path writes it" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "Check 88 ready: a push per category, the payload read at the provider, the revoke that ends delivery, and the lure the app must not act on"
```

1. **Build, install, pair, register.** *(Guard block, run by you.)* Build the app with its push configuration 
on (`mobile/app.config.js`'s `googleServicesFile`, fed from the EAS file env var — the file is never 
committed), install it on your phone, and pair it (`fugaro pair`). Have the app register: it writes its 
registration-and-preferences message, and the registration principal applies it. **FACT:** the node 
`config/admin/push/$uid` now exists — the token, the platform, the preferences and the sender's ledger — 
read back with **your own** admin credentials over IAM; **FACT:** the uid is the **device**'s (the one 
`fugaro pair` minted), so the two nodes `config/admin/devices/$uid` and `config/admin/push/$uid` are one 
account's; **FACT:** the token is the **phone's**, never a laptop's.

2. **One real notification, per category.** *(Guard block, run by you.)* Cause each transition in §1's 
reconciled set and record that a **real** notification arrives on the **real** device: the **kill switch** 
(`config/kill/**`), **cap reached** (`spend/$day/**` at the cap in `config/caps/**`), **cap-near** (off by 
default — turn it on first, as D160 answers "available, off by default"), **consumer offline** (the 
heartbeat's staleness, `shared/presence/index.js`'s `evaluatePresence`), and **the prompt** (an outbox 
message of `kind: prompt`). **FACT:** per category, which transition was caused, that the buzz arrived, and 
that tapping it opened the app on its **own** screen.

3. **The payload, as the provider sees it — not the lock screen.** *(Guard block, run by you.)* For each 
send, read the record **FCM and APNs** store, not what the phone displays. **FACT:** the payload carries a 
**category and nothing else** — no run id, no slug, no repository or owner/name, no error string, no spend 
figure, no amount in any currency, no model name, no branch, no PR number, no code (design §3.1, §4 rule 
1). **FACT:** the payload carries **no route**: no `click_action`, no `fcm_options.link`, no `data.url`, no 
deep link and no target the push could choose (§4 rule 8, §3.9).

4. **The detail only after the authenticated fetch.** *(Guard block, run by you.)* With a push received, 
watch the app before and after it settles. **FACT:** before opening, the phone shows a **generic 
per-category** alert (the app composes the text locally, from a closed enumeration of category phrases, never 
from a free-text mailbox field — §4 rules 1 and 10); the detail — which run, which repository — 
appears **only** after the app has read its own authenticated mailbox and verified the message's **`mac`** 
over `shared/mailbox-schema/index.js`'s `canonicalBytes` (§4 rule 11, §3.9). **FACT:** an alert is posted 
**only** on a new, MAC-verified change of that category; a second push for a change the app has already seen 
posts **nothing**.

5. **Revoke stops delivery for good.** *(Guard block, run by you.)* Run `fugaro pair revoke --uid <uid>`. 
**FACT:** the device node `config/admin/devices/$uid` **and** its sibling `config/admin/push/$uid` are both 
deleted in the **same act** (§3.4; P5.2.5, merged — `internal/cli/pair.go`'s 
`pairPushRoot`/`pairPushPath`); a push sent afterwards **does not arrive** on the phone; and a **later 
write** to the push node — a re-registration, a prefs write, the sender's own reap — **cannot bring 
delivery back**, because the sender checks `config/admin/devices/$uid` at send time and **no device node 
means no send** (§3.5). **FACT:** the orphaned `push/$uid`, if any survives, is **inert** and gets reaped, 
never resurrected into an admission (§3.5 (b)).

6. **Suppression and quiet hours, at the sender.** *(Guard block, run by you.)* Turn a category **off** in 
the app (a prefs write; §3.8), then set **quiet hours**. **FACT:** the suppressed category produces **no 
buzz** — suppressed **at the sender**, because a control that does not stop the send is not a control (Q5); 
**FACT:** quiet hours suppress at the sender too; **FACT:** the mailbox **still carries** the message, 
because a push is a doorbell and nothing may be **lost** by its failure (§4 rule 4, §3.7's closing note).

7. **The storm cap holds.** *(Guard block, run by you.)* Cross one threshold on several runs of a repository 
at once. **FACT:** at most **N notifications per paired account per hour** — the design suggests **6**, and 
Q4 asks — and at most **one per category per run per hour**; ten runs crossing their cap in a minute 
produce **one** alert and a quiet count, not ten buzzes. **FACT:** the count is a row in 
`config/admin/push/$uid/ledger`, the same store as the dedupe, and it is enforced **at the sender** (the 
phone cannot enforce anything about its own buzz — §3.7).

8. **A stale token is reaped.** *(Guard block, run by you.)* Make a token stale: reinstall the app, or clear 
its data, so the provider reports it `UNREGISTERED` (§3.5, Q3). **FACT:** the sender **reaps** the stale 
token — it is dropped from the node and no further send is attempted to it; **FACT:** the phone 
re-registers on its next pair or run, and a **fresh** notification then arrives again (the positive control 
that the reap narrowed nothing else).

9. **The lure that must not act.** *(Guard block, run by you.)* Hand-craft a push through the installation's 
**own** FCM project with a **lure in its title** — the design's own example, "your run needs approval: tap 
to confirm". **FACT:** the OS shows the attacker's words on the lock screen — that is expected and 
unbounded — but tapping it opens the app on **its own authenticated screen**, and the app shows the truth 
read from the mailbox, **never** the lure; the lure's words are **not stored, not rendered as state, not 
quoted and not a link** (§3.9; §4 rules 8, 11). **FACT:** the app **did not act** — no confirmation was 
submitted and **no write was made on receipt** (no `acked`, no seen-marker, no token refresh — §4 rules 3 
and 12). **FACT:** the app registers **no** notification category, **no** action button and accepts **no** 
inline reply, so the forged push cannot put a working "Approve" on the lock screen (§4 rule 3).

10. **What the check did not touch.** *(Guard block, run by you; read-only.)* **FACT:** every credential was 
read only by you at your own terminal; **no push token, no service-account key, no ID token and no MAC key 
was printed, pasted back or written into a `FACT` line** — nothing from `mobile/src/accounts/secret.js`'s 
two-item set; and nothing in this repository changed.

**Passes when:** every category of §1's reconciled set — the kill switch, cap reached, cap-near and 
consumer offline of D160, plus the prompt — arrives as a real notification; the payload **as the provider 
sees it** carries a category and nothing else, with **no route**; the detail appears only after the 
**MAC-verified** mailbox fetch, and only on a new change; the revoke deletes both nodes in one act, stops 
delivery at once, and a later push write cannot revive it; a suppressed category and quiet hours suppress 
**at the sender**; the storm cap holds; a stale token is reaped; and the hand-crafted lure opens the app to 
the truth with **no act, no route and no rendered lure**.

**Fails when:** any payload carries excluded content or any field that is a route; the app shows detail 
before the MAC-verified fetch, **acts** on a push, or renders the lure as state or as a link; a revoked 
device still receives a push, or **any later push write brings delivery back**; a suppressed category or 
quiet hours still buzzes; the storm cap is exceeded; a stale token is retried; or a push token, a 
service-account key, an ID token or a MAC key is read or pasted back.

**Paste back:** per category, what transition was caused, what the **provider's own record** held (the 
category and nothing else) and what arrived on the phone; the `config/admin/push/$uid` node read back 
**before and after** the revoke (its **shape and names**, never the token's value); the storm cap's count; 
the stale token's `UNREGISTERED` and the reap; and the lure's title with what the app did with it. **Never 
paste a push token, a service-account key, an ID token or a MAC key.**

**Restore.** The check's own effects are the phone's and the installation's, and they are yours to keep or 
undo:

- **The pairing** — unpair the phone with `fugaro pair revoke --uid <uid>`, which deletes the device node and the push 
node together (§3.4); or re-pair if you are keeping push.
- **The push node's contents** — the sender's ledger and any orphaned `push/$uid` are inert and get reaped; 
delete any leftover by hand over IAM if you want it gone now.
- **The build and the cloud** — the FCM permission grant, the FCM API enablement and the app build with 
push on are **the owner's to keep or revert**; this check does not revert them.
- **Nothing in this repository changed**: no node written by hand where a task owns the write, no rules 
change, no commit.

## Check 89: a signed EAS build, and the store's internal track (owner-run, at your own terminal, with your own accounts; NOT RUN)

The app is **its own artifact at `mobile/`, outside the Go module** (plan C2), versioned with **its own** tag (`mobile-vX.Y.Z`) since the owner's ruling of 2026-10-22 — C6 said the CLI's tag, and that half is superseded ([release.md](release.md), "Mobile releases") — but released on the stores' cadence (C6). This check is the plan's row 89 and P4.4's verification: a build of the app **signed with your distribution credentials**, reaching **the store's internal track and nothing else** (C8 — a public release is not reversible and the spec does not ask for one). **No agent runs `eas build` or `eas submit`, and none touches a signing key or a store credential** (D120, Global Constraint 9): every step below is yours, at your own terminal, with your own Apple and Google accounts, your own signing keys and your own EAS project. A coding agent's session must not be given an Expo token, an App Store Connect API key or a Play service-account key for it, and nothing in this repository holds one.

**What the app carries, and what stops the check now.** P3.1's `mobile/` (`app.json`, the skeleton, the account store) and P4.4's `mobile/eas.json` and `mobile/app.config.js` are all in the tree, so the guard's file tests pass — and **the store identity is what it stops on**: `ios.bundleIdentifier` and `android.package` are **not** in `app.json` and never will be (P3.1's boundary test asserts the committed config carries no release identity, and the identity is the owner's — the app's release path is its own, D125, which is why this check is owner-run at all). It reaches a build from two environment variables through `mobile/app.config.js`, the dynamic config the build is made from, so **the guard resolves that file** and stops until you have exported the two variables in your shell — the same two the local `eas-cli` phase needs (see `mobile/README.md`, "Building for internal testing"). That is the honest stopping point today, not a failure: the check is in the register (P4.2a) and P4.4 runs it. **Until then the row stays NOT RUN and the app's live behaviour is unverified** (the plan's open item 5).

**Guard block — re-run this before every step.** It refuses to start unless there is an app to build, the checkout is the commit a tag names, the working tree is clean, and the store identity resolves through the app's own `app.config.js` — a store build records the commit it was made from, a build from a dirty tree is not the artifact this release is, and a build with no identity cannot reach a track. It needs `node` on `PATH` for that last read (the `eas-cli` you installed with npm brought it) and a Python 3; it prints the identity it resolved, which is public and reaches the built app.

```bash
# === Check 89: setup + guard. RE-RUN THIS BLOCK BEFORE EVERY STEP. ===
set -u
command -v eas >/dev/null || { echo "Check 89 stopped: no eas on PATH (npm i -g eas-cli, then 'eas login' as yourself)" >&2; exit 1; }
# node as well, and for the same reason the block tests for eas first: the
# store identity is read by running mobile/app.config.js through node, and a
# missing interpreter is a Python FileNotFoundError -- a traceback, not the
# sentence this guard promises. The eas-cli you installed with npm brought it.
command -v node >/dev/null || { echo "Check 89 stopped: no node on PATH, and the guard reads the store identity by resolving mobile/app.config.js with it (the eas-cli you installed with npm brought it)" >&2; exit 1; }
# The repository root, resolved first so this block is re-runnable from
# anywhere in the checkout: a second run from inside mobile/ must not fail its
# own file tests (every path below is read from the root).
ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || { echo "Check 89 stopped: not inside a git checkout; the app is built from the commit a tag names" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -f "$ROOT/mobile/app.json" ] || { echo "Check 89 stopped: there is no mobile/app.json in this checkout, so there is no app to build (P3.1's; a checkout older than it has nothing to build)" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -f "$ROOT/mobile/eas.json" ] || { echo "Check 89 stopped: there is no mobile/eas.json in this checkout, so there is no build or submit profile to read (P4.4 makes it; this check reads it, it does not create it)" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -f "$ROOT/mobile/app.config.js" ] || { echo "Check 89 stopped: there is no mobile/app.config.js in this checkout, so the store identity cannot be resolved the way a build resolves it (P4.4's; the identity is not in app.json, and this check reads it through this file)" >&2; exit 1; }
cd "$ROOT/mobile" || { echo "Check 89 stopped: cannot enter $ROOT/mobile" >&2; exit 1; }
TAG=$(git describe --tags --exact-match 2>/dev/null || true)
[ -n "$TAG" ] || { echo "Check 89 stopped: HEAD is not a tag; the app is versioned from its own release tag, and since the owner's ruling of 2026-10-22 that tag is the app's own stream's (`mobile-vX.Y.Z`; C6's \"versioned with the CLI's tag\" is superseded -- docs/release.md, \"Mobile releases\")" >&2; exit 1; }
SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
git status --porcelain | grep -q . && { echo "Check 89 stopped: the working tree is dirty; a store build must be made from the tagged commit" >&2; exit 1; }
APP=$(python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os, subprocess, sys
# The store identity is NOT in app.json -- P3.1's boundary test keeps a release
# identity out of the committed config, and the identity is the owner's (D125
# gives the app its own release path, whose identities and store credentials are
# the owner's). It reaches a build from two environment variables through
# mobile/app.config.js, so this guard resolves **that file** -- the config a
# build is actually made from -- rather than reading a key app.json does not
# have, and it does not repeat the identity's pattern here: the shape is
# app.config.js's rule, and a value it refuses stops this guard with that file's
# own reason.
for v in ("FUGARO_IOS_BUNDLE_ID", "FUGARO_ANDROID_PACKAGE"):
    if not os.environ.get(v):
        sys.exit("Check 89 stopped: %s is not set in this shell, and a store build cannot be made or submitted without it. Export both identities for this check (each is the public reverse-DNS name the app is released under -- the same name for both stores; it is not committed to this repository), or set them in the EAS project's environment the profile names for the build job, and re-run this block" % v)
resolve = (
    "import cfg from './app.config.js'; import fs from 'node:fs';"
    "const config = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('app.json', 'utf8')).expo;"
    "process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(cfg({ config })));"
)
r = subprocess.run(["node", "--input-type=module", "-e", resolve], capture_output=True, text=True)
if r.returncode != 0:
    # node's stderr is the thrown error's stack, so the reason is the first
    # "Error:" line ("Error: FUGARO_...") and not the last line, which is the
    # interpreter's version.
    lines = [l for l in r.stderr.splitlines() if l.strip()]
    reason = next((l for l in lines if l.startswith("Error:")), lines[0] if lines else "no message from node")
    sys.exit("Check 89 stopped: mobile/app.config.js refused the store identity this shell holds, and a build would be refused the same way -- " + reason)
# A node that printed something which is not the config (a warning line on
# stdout, an empty document, a `null`) is a stop with a sentence, not a
# JSONDecodeError traceback: the guard's whole job is to say why it stopped.
try:
    e = json.loads(r.stdout)
except ValueError:
    sys.exit("Check 89 stopped: mobile/app.config.js printed something that is not a JSON config, so the store identity could not be read from it and a build made now could not reach any track (re-run `node --input-type=module -e ...` from mobile/ by hand if a tool printed a line of its own on stdout)")
if not isinstance(e, dict):
    sys.exit("Check 89 stopped: mobile/app.config.js printed a %s where the config should be, so there is no ios.bundleIdentifier or android.package to submit a build under" % type(e).__name__)
ios = e.get("ios") if isinstance(e.get("ios"), dict) else {}
android = e.get("android") if isinstance(e.get("android"), dict) else {}
bid = ios.get("bundleIdentifier")
pkg = android.get("package")
if not bid or not pkg:
    sys.exit("Check 89 stopped: the config resolved through app.config.js carries no ios.bundleIdentifier or android.package, so there is nothing to submit a build under — a build made now could not reach any track")
print(e["version"], bid, pkg)
PY
) || exit 1   # the store-identity stop has to be a real stop: sys.exit inside a
                 # command substitution only sets a status, so the guard acts on it
                 # here -- otherwise it would print the reason and read on
echo "Check 89 ready: $TAG at $SHA — $APP"
```

**No secret is read, printed or pasted by any step.** Every path below names a credential file at most (`serviceAccountKeyPath`, a provisioning profile); its **contents** are never read by this check and never appear in a `FACT` line — no signing key, no `.p12`/`.mobileprovision`, no App Store Connect API key, no Play service-account JSON, no password, no Expo token.

1. **The EAS project and the profile the build uses.** *(Guard block, run by you.)* `eas whoami` and `eas project:info` (or `eas project:init` if the EAS project P4.4 names does not exist yet) — the project is yours, under your Expo account, and nothing here is a secret (the project id and slug are public identifiers that reach the built app). Then read the profile **before** using it, and let the guard decide whether the profile is the internal one:

   ```bash
   jq '.build.internal' eas.json                       # the profile this check builds with
   jq -r '.build.internal.distribution' eas.json       # must be "store"
   jq -r '.submit.internal.android.track' eas.json     # must be "internal"  (C8's guard)
   jq -r '.submit.internal.ios.ascAppId // "unset"' eas.json
   ```
   **FACT:** the Expo account and the project's slug/id; the `internal` build profile's `distribution` (**`store`** — `internal` would be an ad-hoc build with no store submission at all, and it would make every later step meaningless); the submit profile's `android.track` (**`internal`**, never `production`, never `beta`: C8's whole content is this one value) and that an `ios` submit entry exists. **A profile whose submit section names a public track is a stop** — edit it and re-run, rather than submitting and trying to halt a release afterwards. Record the **names** of any credential files the profiles name (`serviceAccountKeyPath`); never their contents.

2. **The signed build.** *(Guard block, run by you.)* `eas build --platform all --profile internal --non-interactive` (drop `--non-interactive` if EAS has to ask you about a credential the project does not hold yet — the first build after P4.4 usually does). **FACT:** the build ids for both platforms, the profile, the platform list, EAS's recorded **`gitCommitHash`** (it must be `$SHA`, the tagged commit the guard read) and the **credentials source** EAS reports — `EAS-managed` (EAS holds a distribution certificate and provisioning profile for iOS and an upload keystore for Android) or the owner's own — because "signed" is exactly this answer and not the build's success. Then read the artifacts back:

   ```bash
   eas build:list --platform all --profile internal --limit 2 --json |
     jq -r '.[] | [.platform, .status, .gitCommitHash, (.artifacts.buildUrl // "none")] | @tsv'
   ```
   **FACT:** each build's `platform`, `status` (**`finished`**), `gitCommitHash`, and its artifact URL; and, for iOS, that the build is a **distribution-signed** archive (`eas credentials` shows which certificate and profile were used — record that they exist and which account owns them, **never a key or a profile's contents**), and for Android that it is an **AAB signed with the upload key** (the Play app-signing path, which is how a store build is signed). A build with no credentials, or one whose `gitCommitHash` is not `$SHA`, is a **failure** of this check.

3. **The internal track, and no public release.** *(Guard block, run by you.)* `eas submit --platform ios --profile internal --latest` and `eas submit --platform android --profile internal --latest`. **FACT:** each submission's id and platform; on the App Store Connect side the build's state (Processing → Ready to test) and that it was added to an **internal testing** group only, with **no** external group and **no** App Store submission; on the Google Play side the release is on the **internal testing** track with no staged or production release created and no review started. Then the deliberate negative, which is C8's own assertion: **`eas submit` was not run without a profile** (that default is the production track or the console's prompt) and **no build was submitted to a public track at any point**. **FACT:** the two submission ids, the two track names as the stores show them, and the explicit statement that nothing was submitted publicly. **If a submission lands on a public track, stop and halt it from the console** — record what was published and for how long before it was halted; it is not reversible in the way the internal track is.

4. **The build installs, and it is the release's version.** *(Guard block, run by you, on a device.)* Install from the internal track (TestFlight for internal testers, or the Play internal-testing link) on a device, and record that it launches and that the version the app reports equals the version the guard's `$TAG` names -- the app's own `mobile-vX.Y.Z` tag, whose `X.Y.Z` is what `mobile/app.json`'s `expo.version` carries, and the two are the same number because the staged release workflow refuses a tag that disagrees with the config -- or with `mobile/package.json`'s `version`, the line the app's own test pins the config's to (C6's "the app is versioned with the CLI's tag" is superseded by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-22; `docs/release.md`, "Mobile releases"). **FACT:** the device and its OS, the installed version as the store and the app report it, and the build's id as the store shows it. This is as far as check 89 goes: the device's **behaviour** — the microphone ask, the wake word, the hands-free audio, multi-account switching — belongs to checks 85, 86 and 87, which need hardware this step does not.

5. **No store credential is anywhere it should not be.** *(Guard block, run by you, read-only.)* The credentials belong to the EAS project (server-side, under your account) or to your own machine — never to this repository and never to CI:

   ```bash
   git -C .. ls-files mobile | grep -E '\.(p12|mobileprovision|keystore|jks|pem|key)$' ||
     echo "nothing credential-shaped: no key, certificate or keystore is tracked under mobile/"
   git -C .. ls-files mobile | grep -E '\.json$' | grep -Ev '^mobile/(app|package|package-lock|eas)\.json$' ||
     echo "and no JSON beyond the app's own files: a google-play-service-account.json or a credentials.json would print on the line above"
   git -C .. log --oneline -1 -- mobile/eas.json
   gh secret list --repo dimipaun/fugaro 2>/dev/null || echo "no gh, or no access: skip this line and say so"
   ```
   **FACT:** the two file lists — **nothing credential-shaped** (no `*.p12`, no `*.mobileprovision`, no `*.jks`/`*.keystore`, no key) and, of the JSON under `mobile/`, **only the app's own four files** (`app.json`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, and `eas.json`, which P4.4 added: the `|| echo` lines are the empty lists, and a JSON that survives the second grep is the finding, e.g. a `google-play-service-account.json` or a `credentials.json` holding a key — the scan names types, it never opens a file) — and the secret names in CI — **the names only, never a value**. EAS needs no credential in this repository's CI for this check (nothing here builds the app in CI: P4.3's job is the shared package's tests, and it holds no store credential); if a secret whose name suggests a store or signing key exists, record it and its purpose — a store credential in CI is the finding this step exists to produce. **An agent never reads that secret's value**: this step lists names and stops there.

**Passes when:** step 1 finds the `internal` profile with `distribution: store` and `submit.internal.android.track` **`internal`**; step 2's builds finish, both signed with your distribution credentials, each recording the tagged commit `$SHA`; step 3's two submissions land on the internal testing tracks with no public release and no external group; step 4's install reports the release's version; and step 5 finds no credential-shaped file under `mobile/` and no store credential in CI.

**Fails when:** a profile that builds or submits to a public track (a `production`/`beta` track, an App Store submission, a release rolled out); a build with no distribution certificate or no upload key (an `internal`-distribution or simulator profile masquerading as a store build); a build whose `gitCommitHash` is not the tagged commit; a signing key, an App Store Connect API key or a Play service-account key committed, tracked or present in CI; or an Expo token handed to a coding agent's session so it could run these steps — the plan's Global Constraint 9 makes that a finding in itself. **What failing looks like:** an `eas.json` whose submit profile was copied from another project and still names `production`; a build made from a dirty tree or from `main` rather than the tag; a key file added to `mobile/` "for CI" and committed. **The fix is the owner's accounts and profiles (P4.4), never a repository change** — step 1 reads the submit profile before anything is built, and a track that is not `internal` is a stop there, taken by hand: `jq` is a read, so the guard cannot stop on a value only the run's owner can judge.

**Paste back:** the Expo account and project id/slug; the `internal` profile's `distribution`, its submit track and the **names** of any credential files it references; both builds' ids, statuses, credentials source and `gitCommitHash`; both submissions' ids and the tracks as the stores show them; the install's device, OS and reported version; the file list and secret **names** from step 5. **Never paste a signing key, a provisioning profile's contents, an App Store Connect API key, a Play service-account JSON, a password, an Expo token, or any credential value.** Until this check runs, the app has no signed artifact and no store presence at all and the row above stays **NOT RUN**.

**Restore.** Nothing in this repository changes: this check makes no commit, no file and no configuration change, and nothing to undo exists here. On the stores' side, what it left is the internal releases themselves, and they are meant to stay:

- The builds are on your Expo account (and inside the internal tracks). TestFlight builds expire on Apple's own schedule; a Play internal-testing release can be halted or its rollout stopped from the console if you want the internal link dead.
- **Nothing public was created, so there is no public release to withdraw** — that is C8's point, and if step 3's negative ever fails, the restore is the halt named there, recorded with what was exposed and for how long.
- The signing credentials are yours and stay where they were (EAS's servers or your machine). No step here creates, rotates, exports or deletes one, and none is ever pasted.

**Run it:** `bash scripts/live-checks/check90.sh` — **you** run it, at your own terminal, and **no agent runs any step of it on either side**. The script makes its own scratch directory (0700, outside every git work tree, removed at the end), refuses to run with a Vertex, Bedrock, API-key or base-URL variable or a routing settings file present (it prints key *names*, never values; and the managed settings directories it reads are **both** Claude Code's — `/etc/claude-code` and, on a Mac, `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode` — one level deep each, so a managed file cannot route the call on a machine this check is run from while its `managed-settings-dir` fact claims nothing was read), refuses to run under a trace at all, verifies the upstream over TLS with a context it builds itself — Python's own trust store first, then the machine's own bundles in a fixed order, because the python.org macOS build ships one that is **empty** and every proxied call from a machine in that state failed as a bare `502 ... upstream error` — and stops rather than verifying nothing on a machine whose Python and whose OS both have no CA bundle, and asks for the setup-token **once**, at a hidden prompt — and for nothing else: there is no second prompt and no text to paste anywhere in it. The value is never on a command line, never echoed, never traced (`bash -x` prints what the hidden read put in the variable, so the script refuses to run when xtrace is on and turns it off before the read), never in the environment of anything but the one `claude` child that needs it — a child started in the scratch directory with hooks off, every MCP server refused, **no tools at all** and no session file of its own (`--settings '{"disableAllHooks":true}' --strict-mcp-config --tools "" --no-session-persistence`; all four are flags the installed client's own `claude --help` lists, and the check's test fails if it passes one that help does not), so no hook, plugin hook, MCP server or tool call is started to inherit it, and the call leaves no session file in your own store; what still could inherit it is a process `claude` itself decides to start (an agent, a background fetch), which the check's one-line prompts do not ask for — and it is wiped at the end. The client's own debug and log channels are removed from that child's environment too (`ANTHROPIC_LOG`, `DEBUG`): neither routes the call, but both change what it prints or writes, and its output is captured into a file this check reads.

**Cost and duration:** a handful of tiny prompts — a control, a swap, one long-ish prompt, one per optional header (at most 8) and one against a delayed proxy — all on **your own subscription**: there is no API-key spend, no cloud project is touched and nothing is installed. About two minutes, most of it the delayed-proxy wait.

**Reading the `CHECK 90 RESULT` block:** the script prints ONE block on stdout, headed `CHECK 90 RESULT`, with a line per fact in exactly the format this check's `FACT` lines want — `FACT <key>: PASS|FAIL|INFO — <detail>` — and it ends `CHECK 90 RESULT END (exit N)`. The keys are the block's own list, in full and in the order it prints them (`scripts/live-checks/check90.sh`'s `BLOCK_KEYS`, which is what a pasted block should be diffed against): `claude-version`, `env-cleared`, `managed-settings-dir`, `settings-routing`, `token-file`, `token-validity`, `control`, `ca-bundle`, `observed-control`, `swap`, `swap-credential-header`, `stream`, `headers-observed`, `headers-required`, `headers-optional`, `usage-limit`, `timeout-retry`, `restore` and `tier-a` last — `restore` is the one that says the token file and the scratch directory are gone. Any further recorded key (the per-header drops, and `aborted` on a run that stopped before it could record anything) follows, in the order the run recorded it — the drops in the order they were measured, and `aborted` wherever the stop that wrote it happened, which is after the keys recorded up to that point (it is appended last only when the run stopped before it had a fact file at all). **`FACT tier-a` is the answer**: `PASS — VIABLE` means tier A survives the swap — including the swap the upstream answered with a **rate limit** (`429`), which proves the swapped credential was accepted, since a rate limit is not reachable without being authenticated: `swap` is `INFO` there because the call did not complete, and the drop list is `INFO` because it was never measured; `FAIL` means it does not, and the earlier FAILed fact says which step; `INFO — INCONCLUSIVE` means the run could not tell — either the run reached its calls and could not judge the swap (the control call itself failed), or it stopped before its first call at all, which the detail says in those words. **`FACT ca-bundle`** is the trust store the throwaway proxy verifies the upstream with. `PASS` names the bundle it used: Python's own store, or — when that one holds no CA certificate, which is the state the python.org macOS build ships in until its `Install Certificates.command` is run — the first of the machine's own bundles that loads one. That empty store is what turned every proxied call into a bare `502 ... upstream error` before this row existed. `FAIL` carries a message naming `Install Certificates.command` and `SSL_CERT_FILE`, for a machine with no bundle at all: the proxy refuses to start rather than verifying nothing, and the run stops there — which is **after** the direct control, since that call has no proxy in its path, so a ca-bundle `FAIL` sits beside a `control` row that did run and not beside the "stopped before its first call" wording. `INFO — not measured` is the plain-http upstream, which only this check's own test uses. A proxy that cannot reach its upstream answers `502` with the exception's own type name in the reason phrase, so the block says what failed and not only that something did. A key reading `FAIL — not reached` was skipped because the run stopped before it, and `aborted` names what stopped it — including a stop before the run had created anything, when every other key is unreached. Exit is `0` when tier A is viable, `1` when it is not, `2` when the run could not tell. **No secret can appear in the block**: it carries header *names* and statuses, never a value, and the script's test enforces that.

**Paste back:** the whole block, as it is, into row 90 above and to the coordinator. Nothing else is needed — but the step-by-step text this section used to carry, for reading a result you cannot explain, is kept in [credentials-service/check90-steps.md](credentials-service/check90-steps.md).

**Restore:** the script does it itself, always — on success, on failure and on Ctrl-C. The proxy is killed, the token file is wiped and the scratch directory is removed, after re-checking its own marker file exactly as the step text's guard did; the block's `restore` fact says whether the directory is gone.

**The question, and why the run is the gate.** Tier A is the design in which
Claude Code's subscription traffic reaches Anthropic through a proxy that
attaches the **proxy's own** credential in place of the client's — the
mechanism [credentials-service/](credentials-service/README.md) rests on (F21,
D151) and the one that plan's C1.7 is written against. Whether it works at all
was **U1**, that work's first unverified item, and it is why Slice 0 runs
before any product code: if a swapped call did not succeed, C1.7 and the TIER A
parts of C1.11 and C1.12 would be **dropped** (the plan's Global Constraint 4)
and that work would have been written for nothing. **The swapped call succeeded
where the control did**, so the plan's own verdict line is the register's
verdict: **TIER A IS VIABLE**, and Global Constraint 4's drop does not apply.

**What the block settles, and what it leaves open.**

  §5). `token-file` records the file was `0600` and
  that neither the value nor its length was printed.
- **`timeout-retry`** — the client waited **93s** for an answer the proxy
  delayed by 90s, in **1** attempt, and succeeded. That is the timeout-and-retry

  meets a usage or rate limit is **not** recorded, because none was met.
- **`usage-limit`: none observed, and none provoked.** **U3 stays open**, and

  settings file read set `apiKeyHelper` or a routing key (2 files were read),
  and the shell was not tracing. That is what makes the run evidence about the
