# `project policy show --json` prints {"project": ..., "policy": ...}, and `policy` is null
# when none is published: both blocks hang off that inner document, and a read at the top
# level returns null for each of them.
p=d.get("policy") or {}
print("policy published:", d.get("policy") is not None)
print("routing.claude.via:", json.dumps((p.get("routing") or {}).get("claude",{}).get("via")))
print("credentials:", json.dumps(p.get("credentials")))'
   echo "--- the sandbox job: what it mounts, and what it is given ---"
   for J in $(gcloud run jobs list --project="${GCP:?}" --region="${L:?}" --format='value(metadata.name)' \
              | grep -- "${READABLE:?}" | head -3); do
     echo "== $J"
     gcloud run jobs describe "$J" --project="${GCP:?}" --region="${L:?}" \
       --format='yaml(spec.template.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env)' | grep -i 'name:\|secret' || echo "   (no env: describe by hand)"
   done
   fugaro runs ls --repo "$CHK95_SANDBOX_REPO" --since 0 | head -5
   ```
   **FACT:** whether a policy is published at all (**`policy published: false` is a stop** — nothing is published, so there is no switch to read and nothing below can be about the cascade), the policy's `routing.claude.via` (**`cascade`**, or the check has nothing to observe and says so) and its `credentials` block verbatim; per job, the env lines — **no `valueFrom.secretKeyRef` for `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or any model credential**, and (when the gateway runs) `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointing at the gateway rather than at Anthropic — and the last runs listing, which step 3 reads the slug from. **The two blocks are read out of the document's `policy` member and never off its top level**: `project policy show --json` prints `{"project": …, "policy": …}`, so a read at the top level answers `null` for both — and a check that took that `null` for the switch would be reading a pass condition it can never observe. **A model credential still mounted in the job is a failure of this check's first claim**, and it is also why step 2's inspection matters: the mount is the thing that must be gone.

2. **⚠ CONFIRM — the run that inspects its own `/proc`.** *(Guard block.)* One sandbox run, whose task is one command: **the inspection happens inside the job and is read out of the run's own log**, which is the only place it can happen — the job's container exists for the length of the run. The task text is written to be harmless: it changes no file, pushes nothing, opens no pull request of its own, and prints **which** credential variables are *set* per process, never a value.

   ```bash
   fugaro run --repo "$CHK95_SANDBOX_REPO" --run-id "$RID_PROC" --title "check 95: /proc inspection" --task-file - <<'TASK'
   Do not change any file and do not open a pull request. Run exactly this and paste its output verbatim:

   for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do
     [ -r "$p/environ" ] || continue
     n=$(tr '\0' '\n' < "$p/environ" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^\(CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN\|ANTHROPIC_API_KEY\|ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN\|ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL\|GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS\|FUGARO_[A-Z_]*\)=.*/\1/p' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
     [ -n "$n" ] && echo "proc $(basename "$p") sets: $n"
   done
   # and, for the gateway's own token only, whether its value has an Anthropic key's shape --
   # a yes/no, never the value itself:
   tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/self/environ | grep -c '^ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-' || true
TASK
   fugaro logs "$SLUG/$RID_PROC"
   fugaro diagnose "$SLUG/$RID_PROC" | head -40
   ```
   **FACT:** the `proc <pid> sets: …` lines **verbatim** (and the count line for the key's shape), then the run's own outcome. **What must hold:** **no process sets `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`** — the tier-A token is not in the job at all — and **no process carries a model credential's value**: with the gateway on, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is the gateway's own **per-run** token (`internal/agent/env.go`), and the shape line above is how that is told apart from a real key **without ever printing one**; `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at the gateway, not at `api.anthropic.com`. **⚠ On this tree the run cannot get a call served** (the note at the top), so expect the run to end with the gateway's halt rather than with the inspection — record *not observable*, with the halt text, and do not read the absence of the inspection as a pass.
   **This is the one step that costs anything:** a handful of small model calls, tier A and notional (`ModelNotionalUSD`, D140). The other two runs below are refused before any call is served and cost nothing.

3. **The ended run is refused — the write-once outcome, written by you first.** *(Guard block.)* The service admits a run only while the run **has not ended**, and it reads that from `outcomes/<day>/<slug>/<run>` — never from the registry entry, because a run's own token may rewrite that one (D134). So the check writes the outcome itself, **as you, with your own credentials** (IAM bypasses the rules, so this is a hand-write of exactly the node the run's own end would write), and then launches a run with that id: its first call must be refused.

   ```bash
   DAY=$(( $(date -u +%s) / 86400 ))     # budget.DayKey: the UTC epoch day the rules' TODAY computes
   AT=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)  # never printed, never pasted
   curl -fsS -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $AT" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"status":"succeeded","requestedBy":"check95"}' \
     "https://${DBHOST:?}/outcomes/$DAY/$SLUG/$RID_ENDED.json"
   echo                                   # a write of one node; the read-back below is the fact
   curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $AT" "https://${DBHOST:?}/outcomes/$DAY/$SLUG/$RID_ENDED.json"; echo
   # ⚠ CONFIRM: the launch whose first call must be refused
   fugaro run --repo "$CHK95_SANDBOX_REPO" --run-id "$RID_ENDED" --title "check 95: ended run" --task-file - <<'TASK'
   Do not change any file. Reply with one line and stop.
TASK
   fugaro diagnose "$SLUG/$RID_ENDED" | head -30
   ```
   **FACT:** the read-back of the outcome node — the JSON you wrote, `{"status":"succeeded",…}` — and then the run's own end. **What must hold:** the run's calls are **refused** because it has already ended (the service's `RunEnded`, D134) and the run **halts** rather than being served; on this tree the halt is the unreachable-service one, so record **not observable** with its text, and record the outcome node you wrote as the check's own state to delete (step 6). **The node is written for today only**, which is what the service's scan covers: it walks `today+1` down to `launch-1`, where the launch day is the run id's own UTC day, so one hand-written node on the launch day is the whole of the evidence the service reads.

4. **The unreachable service halts the run, and never falls back.** *(Guard block.)* *(Global Constraint 8, D143: no code path mounts a model key in the job when the service is down.)* Make the service unable to serve, launch a run, and read what ended it — then put the service back **before anything else**.

   ```bash
   # ⚠ CONFIRM: the primary route, the plan's own words -- the service at zero instances.
   # This container's gcloud documents `--max-instances=MAX_INSTANCES` as a count of instances and
   # 'default' to remove the override, so a zero value is written here as it is stated and the API
   # may refuse it: record the refusal verbatim if it comes, and take the route below instead.
   gcloud run services update "$SVC" --project="${GCP:?}" --region="${L:?}" --max-instances=0
   # The route that reaches the SAME halt by the same code path, if the API refuses 0: the front
   # end answers 403 before the container, which is `stateDetailUnadmitted` -- a halt, D143:
   #   JOB=$(gcloud run jobs list --project="$GCP" --region="$L" --format='value(metadata.name)' \
   #         | grep -- "$READABLE" | head -1)
   #   JOB_SA=$(gcloud run jobs describe "$JOB" --project="$GCP" --region="$L" \
   #            --format='value(spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName)')
   #   gcloud run services remove-iam-policy-binding "$SVC" --project="$GCP" --region="$L" \
   #     --member="serviceAccount:$JOB_SA" --role=roles/run.invoker
   # ⚠ CONFIRM: the launch
   fugaro run --repo "$CHK95_SANDBOX_REPO" --run-id "$RID_DOWN" --title "check 95: service down" --task-file - <<'TASK'
   Do not change any file. Reply with one line and stop.
TASK
   fugaro runs ls --repo "$CHK95_SANDBOX_REPO" --since 1h | head -5
   fugaro diagnose "$SLUG/$RID_DOWN" | head -40
   fugaro logs "$SLUG/$RID_DOWN" | tail -20
   # RESTORE IMMEDIATELY, before reading anything else:
   gcloud run services update "$SVC" --project="${GCP:?}" --region="${L:?}" --max-instances=default
   #   ... or, on the binding route:  gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding "$SVC" \
   #     --project="$GCP" --region="$L" --member="serviceAccount:$JOB_SA" --role=roles/run.invoker
   gcloud run services get-iam-policy "$SVC" --project="${GCP:?}" --region="${L:?}" --format=json \
     | python3 -c 'import json,sys
for x in json.load(sys.stdin).get("bindings",[]):
    if x["role"]=="roles/run.invoker": print("invoker ->", ", ".join(x["members"]))'
   ```
   **FACT:** the halt the run recorded — its `reason` **`budget_unavailable`** (`runstore.HaltBudgetUnavailable`) and the detail the gateway writes: **`the credentials service could not be reached`** for the zero-instance route, or **`the credentials service refused this job's call (check the job's invoker grant on the service)`** for the binding route — read from `fugaro diagnose` / `fugaro runs ls`, verbatim. **What must hold:** the run **halts** and **no call is answered from a credential of the job's own** — which is also what step 2's inspection already proved is not in the job at all — and the service is **back** (the invoker listing printed above, or `--max-instances` back to its value). **A run that kept working with the service down would be the failure this step exists for.** Note that a `run` whose job is still starting takes a couple of minutes to reach its first call; `fugaro runs ls` is where its status appears.

5. **What the run's own record carries.** *(Guard block, read-only.)* Once the service serves, the run's record is where D140's per-call accounting shows: the **credential's name** and the tiers.

   ```bash
   fugaro diagnose "$SLUG/$RID_PROC" | sed -n '/credential/,+6p'
   fugaro runs ls --repo "$CHK95_SANDBOX_REPO" --since 0 | head -10
   ```
   **FACT:** the credential's **name** (never a value) and the tier lines the record carries — `byTier.b` / `byTier.c` real spend under `runs/$slug/$run` and `spend/$day/…`, with tier A on the `notional` nodes (D140, Check 92's own children). **⚠ Not observable on this tree** (no call is served): record it as such.

6. **What survives: nothing of the check's own — the final assertion.** *(Guard block.)* Three runs, their task objects, and one hand-written outcome node are everything this check creates.

   ```bash
   DAY=$(( $(date -u +%s) / 86400 ))
   AT=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)   # never printed, never pasted
   for R in "$RID_ENDED" "$RID_DOWN" "$RID_PROC"; do
     curl -fsS -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $AT" "https://${DBHOST:?}/runs/$SLUG/$R.json" >/dev/null 2>&1
     curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $AT" "https://${DBHOST:?}/runs/$SLUG/$R.json"; echo "   # want null ($R)"
   done
   for D in $DAY $((DAY - 1)); do
     curl -fsS -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $AT" "https://${DBHOST:?}/outcomes/$D/$SLUG/$RID_ENDED.json" >/dev/null 2>&1
   done
   curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $AT" "https://${DBHOST:?}/outcomes/$DAY/$SLUG/$RID_ENDED.json"; echo "   # want null"
   fugaro runs ls --repo "$CHK95_SANDBOX_REPO" --since 0 --json \
     | grep -c -e "$RID_PROC" -e "$RID_ENDED" -e "$RID_DOWN"     # 0
   gcloud run services describe "$SVC" --project="${GCP:?}" --region="${L:?}" \
     --format='value(spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName)'      # the credentials account, unchanged
   ```
   **FACT:** each read-back — **`null`** for the three run nodes and the outcome node (both the day you wrote and the day below it are deleted, because the service scans both) — the run-listing count **`0`**, and the service's account line unchanged. **The `0` is the assertion this register's checks all end on**: a `grep -c` that finds nothing of the check's own.

**Passes when:** the guard's ready line names `fugaro` on `fugaro-dev`, the sandbox repository and the three run ids; step 1 shows `routing.claude.via: cascade` and no job mounting a model credential; step 2's log (once the service serves) shows **no `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in any process**, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at the gateway, and no process carrying an Anthropic-shaped key; step 3's run is refused because its outcome is already written; step 4's run halts with reason **`budget_unavailable`** and the unreachable/unadmitted detail, and the service is restored; step 5 shows the credential's name and the tier lines in the record; step 6 reads **`null`** and **`0`**.

**Fails when:** a job still mounts a model credential (step 1), or a process inside the run sets `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` or carries an Anthropic-shaped `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (step 2); the ended run is **served** rather than refused (step 3); the run keeps working with the service unreachable, or is answered from a key of the job's own (step 4) — **that is the Global-Constraint-8 failure**; or a run node or the outcome node is left behind (step 6).

**Paste back:** the guard's ready line, the two typed variables **names** (never a value), and `fugaro version`; step 1's policy lines, the jobs' env lines and the runs listing; step 2's `proc <pid> sets:` lines verbatim and the key-shape count, with the run's own end; step 3's outcome read-back and the refusal; step 4's `gcloud` output (including a verbatim refusal if the API refused `--max-instances=0`), the halt's reason and detail from `diagnose`, and the restored invoker listing; step 5's credential/tier lines or the record that they were not observable; step 6's three `null`s and the `0`. **Names, principals and counts — never a token, a key, an environment value or a secret's payload.**

**Restore.** The state this check leaves is the state later checks expect, with exactly one exception — the service must be **serving again**:

- **The service.** Put it back the moment step 4 is read: `--max-instances=default` (which removes the override, the shape the installation's Terraform leaves), or re-add the `roles/run.invoker` binding for the job account. **Do not leave it unreachable**: Checks 96 and 99 both launch sandbox runs, and every one of them would halt exactly as step 4's did.
- **The three runs and the outcome node.** Step 6 deletes them and reads them back `null`; if you stopped before it, do it by hand — `runs/<slug>/<rid>` for the three ids (the task objects a launch wrote) and `outcomes/<day>/<slug>/<RID_ENDED>` on **both** the day you wrote and the day below it. A delete is an owner write (IAM), which is what makes it possible at all: no run token may write either node.
- **Nothing else.** No rules, no policy, no mark, no credential: this check writes no cascade state, reads no value, and never opens the bundle. The one thing it reads that is not its own is the run's own log, which Cloud Logging keeps on its own schedule.
- **The audit config Check 94 turned on** stays on; nothing here touches it.


## Check 96: GitHub tokens through the service — the job holds no App key, the mint is the service's for one repository with the run's permissions, and a run identity for repository X cannot mint for Y (`fugaro-dev` only, never `belong`; run by you; NOT RUN)

**DRAFT: read the whole of this preamble before running it.** The owner ruled on 2026-10-22 that only critical and major findings block the release and that every owner-run check follows it. This check was reviewed a third time for exactly the readings its earlier drafts got wrong, and this revision corrects them: the operator's stop switches are **not** the first database read of a call (the identity verification reads the run's write-once outcome first, `internal/credsvc/auth.go`'s `checkLive`, and a denied read there is what answers `state_unavailable`); the pairing refusal is **not** answered before any database read (it needs a verified identity, and verification is what makes that read — so the pairing refusal is answered only by a service whose database reads are admitted, which since 0.10.1 this one's are, its account holding its own two-permission database role; while its other half, a caller that is no job account, is refused out of the configured table before any read, and is observable with or without that role); and the issuance line **is** written on the forward path (`internal/credsvc/cascade.go`'s `answer`), so the refusals this check expects to be recorded are recorded. What remains true is that the service mints only from a bundle the operator has filled (`fugaro creds set github-app-key` is its only writer; no Terraform writes it), and that the App key's drop (C2.3) is held. It is the live half of 0.10.1, which wires the service end to end — the runner half is on `main` as of that release, the drop (C2.3) is held, and this check is the live result the drop waits on — so run it for what it reads, and read a refusal this preamble names as the expected state of this tree as the state of this tree rather than as a finding.

**NOT RUN.** Written by Task C2.4 of [credentials-service/implementation-plan.md](credentials-service/implementation-plan.md) (its Check 96, D145 and F34; tasks C2.1–C2.4, whose runner half is C2.2's and whose drop is C2.3's). **No step of it has been run, and nothing here is a claim that it works.** It is the live half of the one change that moves the GitHub App's private key out of the job and into the credentials service's bundle (D145): C2.1 mints at the service, C2.2 makes the runner ask for the token there, C2.3 takes the job's grant and its mount away, and this check is what reads the three results on a real installation. Its offline halves are `internal/credsvc`'s mint tests, `internal/gitprov/github`'s service-token tests and `internal/config`'s held-secrets tests; this is the half that needs a deployed service, a job and a real GitHub installation.

**What is not true on this tree, stated plainly, because it decides whether this check can run at all.** Three independent things have to be in place before a single row of the block below means anything, and **none of them is in place on this branch**:

- **C2.3's drop has not landed, and the owner holds it deliberately.** C2.3's drop reads one switch, `config.ServiceHeldSecretNames` (`internal/config/providers.go`), and **on this tree that list is empty**: every job still mounts `FUGARO_GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and its account still holds the accessor on it. So the `app-key` row's first question — does the job's spec name the App key — is answered **yes, it still does**, and that is the honest answer rather than a failure of the release: the flip waits on **this check's own live result** (the owner's live Check 96 has to prove the deployed service mints before the grant and the mount come off, which is #907), and it is the release after the one that wires the runner. **This check runs before the drop, by design**: what the `app-key` row records is the grant and the mount still there, the variable now on a repository job's execution, and the runner reading no key — the state the flip is made safe from.
- **The runner's keyless path is switched on by the launch, on a repository's own job and on the shared project job a switched profile sends its runs to.** `internal/gitprov/providers/providers.go` opens the github provider without a key — and mints nothing in-job — only when the job's environment carries `FUGARO_CREDENTIALS_SERVICE_URL`, the "this installation has a credentials service" fact (D146/D147). **The launch is what puts it there, as of 0.10.1**: `internal/cli/run.go`'s `credentialsServiceLaunchEnv` reads the installation's own record of the service — the URL the credentials stage wrote into the project's config, which the published shared config carries to every machine — and sets it on the execution's environment, so on a **switched-on repository a per-repository job's spec carries the name** and its runner opens the provider keyless. A **shared project job** is judged by the *same* switch, not a different one (B5.1, B5.2, D505, D2078): `credentialsServiceLaunchEnv` decides its address from the repository the run is for, exactly as it decides a repository's own job's, because the service admits a shared caller for the repositories its profile admits (G21, F40) — the rule that refused the class whole (Global Constraint 6) is the one B5.1 replaced — and the job keeps every mount it has (G17: the address arrives first and the drop is B5.7's flip). The one exception the code makes is where the document the run will use cannot be read: a repository's own job is told anyway, because its mounts are already gone, while a shared job's is withheld, because it still holds every mount. **What to expect on a switched-on repository is therefore `FUGARO_CREDENTIALS_SERVICE_URL` present on a per-repository job's execution and, on the same switch, on the shared project job's, and the App key not read in-job; on any job of a repository whose root has **not** been re-applied with the switch on, the variable is absent** and the job reads the key and mints in-job exactly as before. **What a told shared job then meets is the class's own missing deployment**: its table is `FUGARO_SHARED_JOB_ACCOUNTS`, read by the service's own binary and rendered by no module under `deploy/terraform/` yet (`internal/infra/tf`'s `CredentialsServiceEnvAwaitingTheModule` carries the name ahead of its module), so every deployed service starts with an empty shared set and refuses the class whole — the caller falling through to the per-repository table — and a shared job's GitHub run halts at the service's door rather than being served (D143). This check reads that table off the deployed revision too (`FUGARO_SHARED_JOB_ACCOUNTS` in the service's container environment, reported in the `service` row) and stops on a shared project job rather than judging the rows below it: the mint, the pairing and the audit lines all call as the job's own account, and for a shared one they would read that refusal and nothing about the release.
- **The service is configured from its own deployment now, and reads the installation's database.** `fugaro credentials serve` (C1.14) builds its whole configuration out of the environment the installation module sets on its container — **the seven names** `credentials.tf` carries (`deploy/terraform/gcp/modules/installation/credentials.tf`), which are exactly `internal/cli/credentials_serve.go`'s `credentialsServiceEnvNames` and `internal/infra/tf`'s `credentialsServiceEnv` allow-list — so a revision of this release starts, and that gap is closed. And since 0.10.1 its account holds **two** grants: `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor` on the bundle container (Q6, `credentials.tf`), and its **own database role** — the custom role `fugaroCredentialsDatabase`, declared in the Firebase project the database lives in, holding exactly `firebasedatabase.instances.get` and `firebasedatabase.instances.update` (the database's two data permissions, and no instance lifecycle), bound to that account and no other, with no `condition` (ledger #903; RTDB IAM has no path-level scope for a condition to fence). Every read a call makes of the database is therefore **admitted**, not denied: the first one is **not** the stop switches but the identity verification's own read of the run's write-once outcome (`internal/credsvc/auth.go`'s `checkLive`, reached from `Auth.Verify` before `ServeHTTP` asks anything else), and the stop switches (`internal/credsvc/server.go`'s `Kills.Stop`), the policy and the bundle all come after it and are read by the same role. **So a call is no longer stopped at the database on this tree, and both of the block's refusal rows are observable**: **(a) and (b) are both observable**, because the pairing question is asked only after `Auth.Verify` returned a whole identity and that verification now completes, and (b) is still the first of the two — `verifyJob` refuses a caller that is no job account out of the account table the container was configured with (`internal/credsvc/auth.go`, the first thing `Auth.Verify` does), before any database read, answering `403` `unverified_job_identity` — through `refuseIdentity`, which writes no line because no identity was verified to record. What a mint call meets now is the service's own next dependency rather than a database denial: the bundle it mints from is written by no Terraform and no step of this check (`fugaro creds set github-app-key` is its only writer), so a mint against a bundle the operator has not filled is refused there, with the bundle loader's own sentence (`the credentials bundle is absent`) — the wire status is `state_unavailable` again, which is what every refusal of this endpoint carries (`internal/credsvc/github.go`'s `refuseMint`), but the message and the audit line are the bundle's and not the run's-outcome read's. **And a per-repository job the launch gives `FUGARO_CREDENTIALS_SERVICE_URL`** (the bullet above) asks this service, so on a switched-on repository a GitHub run's mint is the service's — refused at the bundle the same way until the operator has written the App key into it.

**What the check is a statement about, and what decides each part.** The three claims of the plan's row 79, each with the code behind it, because a check that reads a claim without its mechanism is a check that cannot tell a regression from a rename:

- **The job holds no App key.** The drop is C2.3's and it is driven by `config.ServiceHeldSecretNames`: `internal/infra/spec.go` and `readiness.go` build the job's secret mounts from that list, `modules/workflow/sa.tf`'s `job_mounts` and `job.tf`'s container environment are the Terraform half, and the accessor grant the job account used to hold on the App key's container is what the same flip removes. The check reads all three as they are deployed — never from the Terraform in the checkout, which is the intent and not the state.
- **The run's installation token is minted by the service, for one repository, with the run's permissions.** `credsvc.MintPath` = `POST /v1/github/installation-token`; the request type carries the App's ID and **nothing else** — there is no repository field to fill in, which is what makes the repository a property of the service rather than of the caller — and the repository is `JobAccount.Repo`, the canonical name the calling job's account is bound to (`JobAccountsFor`); the permissions are `github.RunTokenPermissions`, the exported spelling of the set the in-job provider mints with, so the two paths cannot drift into asking GitHub for different reaches on one run; and the answer carries the token, its expiry and that repository's name.
- **A run identity for repository X cannot mint for Y.** `ServeHTTP` verifies the two identities separately and then asks the pairing question itself: `ja, bound := s.jobs[id.JobAccount]; if !bound || ja.Slug != id.Slug` answers `403` `unverified_run_identity` with *"the run identity is not a run of the calling job's repository"* (review finding N1 — C1.10 pairs nothing, so the pairing is an admission question). A caller whose account is in no row of the table is refused `unverified_job_identity` by `verifyJob`, and that refusal is what makes Cloud Run IAM's invoker grant a fence and not the whole gate.

**How this check makes a mint call at all.** The service admits nobody else, so the check has to present the two identities a launcher's gateway presents, and it builds both itself: the **caller's** Google ID token for the service's URL, read by impersonating the sandbox job's own account (`gcloud auth print-identity-token --impersonate-service-account=… --audiences=… --include-email`), which needs `iam.serviceAccounts.getOpenIdToken` on that account — a permission the installation's own grants deliberately do not give operators (`modules/workflow/sa.tf` grants `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser`, which is `actAs` and nothing else), so this is where the check stops with that permission named if your credential does not hold it. The `outsider` row reads a **second** caller token the same way, from an account that is no job account of this installation (the token signer): it has to be a service account, because this route's class keeps the service's URL as the token's audience (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-04 lets the plain token a user account mints in for the **person** class alone, `internal/credsvc/auth.go`'s `GcloudAudience`) and gcloud refuses `--audiences` outright for a user account — while `--include-email` is the flag an impersonated mint needs for its `email` claim to be there at all. Then the **run's** Firebase ID token, minted with the installation's token signer and exchanged for a live identity exactly as `internal/budget/token` does it — a custom token whose claims are `MintAt`'s (`iss`/`sub` the signer, `aud` the Identity Toolkit audience, `iat`/`exp`, `uid` `r~<slug>~<run>`, and `claims` {`fs`, `fr`, `fx` in milliseconds, `fp`, `rb`}), signed with `gcloud iam service-accounts sign-jwt` (the `fugaroTokenMinter` grant Check 92's helper uses, and the same restricted web API key), then traded at `accounts:signInWithCustomToken`. Run ids are the launcher's own form (`YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<4 hex>`), because the service places a run by its id (`runDay`) and must find no write-once outcome for it — which is also why every identity this check mints is **live** and every one of them is a scratch uid the check deletes.

**What this check holds, and where it never goes.** Two things it holds are credentials: the custom tokens and ID tokens it mints, and — in the `mint` row only — the one real GitHub installation token the service answers with. Every one of them lives in a shell variable or in the script's own scratch directory (mode `0700`) and nowhere else: **no token is echoed, written to the repository, or passed in an argument** (curl reads all of its Authorization headers from stdin, through `--config -`, so no token reaches `ps`), and the block it prints greps its own text for `ghs_` — the fixed prefix of every GitHub installation token — because a check whose FACT lines could carry a token would be the leak it exists to rule out. The minted installation token is never used for a write: the `reach` row's probes are two reads and one request against a workflow name that does not exist, which GitHub refuses before anything could dispatch. `Belong` is never touched by the script (D147), and nothing it does reads the bundle, the database's credential nodes or any secret value.

**Run it:** `bash scripts/live-checks/check96.sh [--dry-run] [--workflow <name>] [<owner/name>]` — one command, in the shape of `check90.sh` and `check91.sh`, and not a list of steps. It derives everything it can — the installation, its job, the service's URL, the Firebase project, the token signer, and the second repository the pairing case needs — from `fugaro doctor`, the installation's own config file (which is where the Firebase project, the token signer and the restricted web API key are read), `fugaro budget show --all --json` and gcloud. The one thing it will not derive for you is **which repository is the sandbox**: what it mints there is a *real* GitHub installation token for the repository it is handed and what it reads at GitHub is that repository, so with state for more than one repository and none named it stops (exit `2`) and lists them rather than picking one — name it, that is the one word this check asks for. It reads the repository out of the installation's own state only where that state holds exactly one repository — and there it stops in that same step, with the `installation` row unmeasured and the block saying so, because the second repository the pairing case needs is not in the state — so the command you run names one. The second thing it will not derive is **which workflow's job to read** where the sandbox repository's `fugaro.yaml` has several: it has one job per workflow, and which of them a run lands on is what `fugaro run --workflow` answers (`internal/cli/run.go`'s `resolveWorkflow`), so name the workflow too — `--workflow <name>` is the value the job wears as its `fugaro_workflow` label, which for a named OAuth account is that account's token joined to the workflow (`gcp.WorkflowVariant`: `go_belong` is the workflow `go` on the account `belong`). With several jobs of its own and no flag the check stops (exit `2`) on one line — naming what it found and ending with `Re-run with --workflow <one of: …>` — rather than read one of them and report its account, its environment and its mint as the repository's; a name no job of the repository carries is refused the same way, in one line listing the labels it did find. That installation is `dimipaun/fugaro`'s, whose two jobs carry `go` and `go_belong`: `go` is the one to name, and **a workflow of the owner's own `belong` account is refused by name** before a single call — and so is a job whose own service account is one, refused before the first `curl` so that no mint goes out as it. It refuses the `belong` project and anything that is not the `fugaro` installation on `fugaro-dev` before it makes a single call — the installation is read by **name**, not by its project alone, because the Firebase project, the token signer and the web API key it mints its run identities with all come out of that one config, so another installation sharing `fugaro-dev` is not this check's and mints nothing here — refuses to run inside a git work tree, keeps its scratch directory at mode `0700` with a marker of its own, and removes it on the way out. **No agent runs it, and no agent runs any part of it.**

```bash
bash scripts/live-checks/check96.sh acme/sandbox                     # the check itself: the repository you name is the one the mint is made for
bash scripts/live-checks/check96.sh acme/sandbox --workflow go       # a repository whose fugaro.yaml has several workflows: the job of the workflow you name (its fugaro_workflow label) is the one read
bash scripts/live-checks/check96.sh acme/sandbox --dry-run           # guards and reads only, then the plan of what a real run would do: exit 0, nothing that writes
bash scripts/live-checks/check96.sh                                  # no repository named: only for an installation whose state holds exactly one, which is then the sandbox
```

**Exit codes, and what a stopped run means.** `0` — every row of the block passed. `1` — at least one row failed, and the block is the finding: a `1` is not "the check broke", it is the answer this check exists to produce. `2` — the check could not tell: a guard refused (the wrong project, a name that belongs to another installation, a shell started with tracing on), the sandbox repository could not be named (several repositories have state and none was named: the message lists them, and naming one is the whole fix), a tool was missing, the service or the job was not there, or a read it needs (the service's log, GitHub, the job's own document) did not answer. A stopped run prints the row that stopped it, marks every row it never reached `FAIL — not reached` — they were **not** measured, which is what the exit code says — and its `restore` row names what happened to the scratch directory and to the run identity users its exchanges may have created.

**A row that reads the service's log waits for it, and waits about ninety seconds at most.** Cloud Logging is eventually consistent: the line the service wrote a moment ago is usually readable within seconds and sometimes is not, and a read taken too early answers an empty document. Empty is exactly what the `audit` and `pairing` rows read as *"the service answered this call and left it unrecorded"* — the one finding those two rows exist to report — so a check that read once would report the finding on a service that is behaving, on the very result the App-key drop (#907) waits on. Both rows therefore re-read the run's lines until the line the call should have written is there: up to `CHECK96_LOG_TRIES` (18) reads `CHECK96_LOG_POLL` (5) seconds apart, about 90 seconds, and only a line that never arrives fails the row. A run that sits still for a moment at one of those two rows is waiting for the log to catch up, and it says so on stderr (`… reading again in 5s`) while it waits.

**Reading the `CHECK 96 RESULT` block:** the script prints one block, one `FACT <key>: <verdict> — <detail>` line per key, in a fixed order, so that a block you paste can be diffed against the next run and a row a stopped run never reached reads `FAIL — not reached` instead of going missing: **`installation`** — the installation the config in force describes (GCP project, region, the Fugaro project, the token signer and that a restricted web API key is present, never the key), the sandbox repository it read and whether you named it or it derived it, and the second repository the pairing case needs; **`service`** — the service labelled `fugaro_role=credentials`, its URL, its own account, the `FUGARO_PROJECT` its container names (which is the run identity's `fp` claim) and whether its container carries `FUGARO_SHARED_JOB_ACCOUNTS`, the shared class's own table, which decides whether a shared project job can be read past its `job-env` row; **`job`** — the sandbox repository's own job, found by its `fugaro_repo` label, the account it runs as and its `FUGARO_GITHUB_APP_ID` — or, when the repository has **no** job of its own, the installation's shared project job, which is what the `job-env` row then reports. A repository with **several** jobs of its own (one per workflow of its `fugaro.yaml`) is neither, and is told the same way a run is: `--workflow <name>` reads the job that wears that name as its `fugaro_workflow` label, and the row then reports that job — the name being `gcp.WorkflowVariant`'s key for the workflow, so a named OAuth account's job is its workflow joined to the account — while the rows below judge that job's account, that job's environment and the mint made as it. With several jobs and no flag, and with a name no job of the repository carries, it stops (exit `2`) on one line rather than read one of them and report its account, its environment and its mint as the repository's: the refusal names the labels it found — each job's own name with the workflow label that tells it apart — and the several-and-no-flag half ends with the fix, `Re-run with --workflow <one of: …>`. A workflow of the owner's own `belong` account is refused by **name** before any call, and so is a job whose own service account is one, refused before the first request goes out; **`job-env`** — the job's environment **names**, its mounts and its secret references (names only, never a value), held to the launch: the expected answer on a switched-on repository's repository job is `true` for `FUGARO_CREDENTIALS_SERVICE_URL` (the variable is what opens the github provider keyless), while a repository job whose root has not been re-applied with the switch on legitimately reads `false` there, and a `true` on one of those is a finding: the job and the config in force have moved apart (the repository's own record is read out of the config's `repos` mapping at the indentation fugaro writes that file with — `yaml.v3`'s four spaces — so `unset` here means the config carries no such repository rather than a key this check could not find). On a **shared project job** the same switch judges it (B5.2), so the expected answer there is `true` on a switched-on repository and `false` on one whose root has not been re-applied — the row is judged against the config in force for both jobs alike, and its message names which job it read — and that job is then where the run **stops** (exit `2`): the `service` row reports whether the deployed revision carries `FUGARO_SHARED_JOB_ACCOUNTS`, and with that name absent no module under `deploy/terraform/` renders the class's table yet, so every row below the `job-env` one would be reading the class's own refusal rather than the release — which is a statement about a deployment and not a finding about the wiring this check measures; **`app-key`** — the first claim: the checkout's own `config.ServiceHeldSecretNames` line, the deployed job's environment, mount and accessor grant, and the consistency of the two, which is the four pairs the bullet above lists; **`bundle`** — Q6: the bundle's container and its policy, exactly one `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor` binding whose one member is **read** to be the service's own account rather than assumed from the count (the row prints `the service's own account among them: <yes|no>`), no condition and no second member, and the job account a member of it: `no`; **`front-end`** — the mint path called with **no identity at all**, refused `403` before the container runs, with no audit line gained for it, and read so that the two `403`s cannot be taken for one another: the same status and the same unmoved line count are also what a service deployed **without Cloud Run IAM** leaves, where the call reaches the container and is refused at the shared header parse — a call with no `Authorization` header at all fails `RequestFromHTTP`, and `internal/credsvc/server.go` answers that through `refuse` with `403` `unverified_run_identity` and no line either (nothing was verified to record), so this row reads the **body** the call came back with — the front end's own non-JSON refusal is the pass and the service's typed one is the finding — and it compares only two counts it actually read: a log read this check cannot parse is a read that did not answer (exit `2`, with the row marked not reached), never two counts that were never taken and compare equal as empty strings; **`mint`** — the run's own call, made with the caller's ID token (the sandbox job's own account) and a run identity of the repository's own slug, answered `200` with `repository` the run's own repository and an expiry inside the hour, and with the request carrying no field in which a caller could have named another; **`reach`** — the minted token read **at GitHub**, which is the only place a token's reach can be read: the installation's repository list holds exactly that one repository, a `contents` read answers `200`, and an `actions: write` probe answers `403`; **`audit`** — the service's own log for this run: exactly one line, `credential` `github-app-key` (the name, never a value), `purpose` `mint`, no tier, `status` `ok`, and no `ghs_` anywhere in it; **`pairing`** — the third claim: the same job account with a run identity of the **other** repository is refused `403` `unverified_run_identity` with *"the run identity is not a run of the calling job's repository"* and nothing minted, and the refusal **is** audited — **exactly `1` audit line for the pairing refusal's run id**, `purpose` `mint`, `credential` `github-app-key`, no tier, `status` `unverified_run_identity`, `repository` the RUN's own and not the calling job's. The line is what tells an answer on `refuseCall`'s path from one on `refuse`'s: `refuseCall` is the one which writes one line through `auditCall` and only then the typed refusal, because the pairing question is asked only after `Auth.Verify` returned a whole identity — so **A `0` here would be the finding**, a refusal this service made and left unrecorded; **`outsider`** — a caller that is no job account of the installation at all (the token signer, the one non-job account this check already acts as): refused `403` by Cloud Run's own front end with no line for the call, which is the stock installation (its only invoker grants are the job accounts' own), or `403` `unverified_job_identity` by the service itself if that account holds `run.invoker` on it — a debugging grant nothing in the installation makes for you — and a `200` is the finding either way; **`survivors`** — the last step: the Firebase Auth users this run's exchanges may have created are deleted and the project's own user list is read back — **every page of it**, and only a read that answered `200` is a read at all, because a read-back that went out without a token or stopped at the first page would count a project holding all of them as a project holding none — and the read-back count (**`0`** of their uids) is the assertion, not the deletions; **`xtrace`** — that this shell was not started with `-x`, which would put a token it read into the log you paste; and **`restore`** — the scratch directory's fate, which of the three facts about the run identity users it is — the list read back and holding none of them, the list read back and still holding some, or the list **never read back**, in which case the row names the uids the run may have created and the one call that deletes each, rather than calling them gone — and the one thing no run can take back (the minted installation token, which GitHub expires on its own). A `secret-scan` row appears only when the block's own text carried the fixed prefix of a GitHub installation token: the line that carried it is dropped and the block fails, because that is this check failing on its own hygiene rather than a fact about the installation.

**What it never prints, and what it restores.** Every call carries its credential in a `curl` config read from stdin (`--config -`), so no token ever reaches `argv` or `ps`; the tokens live in shell variables and in a mode-`0700` scratch directory that is removed at the end; and the block scans its own text for `ghs_` before it prints. Nothing else changes: the script deploys nothing, applies no Terraform, writes no database node, reads no bundle and changes no job. The Firebase Auth users it creates (one per run identity it exchanges, `r~<slug>~<run>` under this check's own run ids) are deleted in its last step, and the project's own user list is read back — every page of it, on a `200` — holding none of their uids; a run that stops before that step, or whose read-back did not answer, leaves those users named by uid in the `restore` row together with the one call that deletes each of them, because a list this check did not read is not a list it can call empty — and a uid goes down before the exchange is attempted and not after it answered, since the user is made *by* the exchange: an answer that never arrived is a user that exists and that nothing would otherwise name.

**Passes when:** the `installation`, `job`, `job-env`, `app-key` and `bundle` rows hold for the state the checkout is in — `config.ServiceHeldSecretNames`'s own line is recorded, and the job's spec is read against it: **on this release the list is empty (the held drop), so the job's container environment still names `FUGARO_GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and its account still holds the accessor** — that is the expected answer and not a failure — while the release that fills the list is the one where the same two facts must read false, with no mount or secret reference of the job's spec naming the App key's container; on either, the job's account is a member of neither the App key's policy nor the bundle's, `FUGARO_CREDENTIALS_SERVICE_URL` is present on a switched-on repository's **per-repository** job's execution and absent on every other — a shared project job's, and any job of a repository whose root has not been re-applied with the switch on (a `true` on either is a finding: the variable is what opens the provider keyless, so a job that carries it while the config in force does not record the repository as switched on is the job and the record having moved apart, which is what `job-env` fails) — and the bundle's policy is exactly the one `secretmanager.secretAccessor` grant on the service's own account (Q6); the `front-end` row's unauthenticated call is refused `403` by the front end with no audit line (the platform's own answer, not the service's typed refusal — the body is what says which); the `mint` row answers `200` naming the sandbox repository, expires inside the hour, and its token reaches exactly that one repository, reads `contents` (`200`) and is refused `actions: write` (`403`), with one audit line for the run — `credential` `github-app-key`, `purpose` `mint`, no tier, `status` `ok` — and no `ghs_` anywhere in the log; the `pairing` and `outsider` rows' two refusals are `403` `unverified_run_identity` (the pairing sentence, with **exactly one** audit line for it — `purpose` `mint`, `credential` `github-app-key`, no tier, `status` `unverified_run_identity`, `repository` the RUN's own: the refusal is made after the identity was verified, so `refuseCall` records it before it answers) and, for a caller that is no job account, a `403` from the front end with no audit line (the stock installation, whose request never reaches the container) or `403` `unverified_job_identity` from the service if that account holds `run.invoker` — neither minting anything, and only the second of those two answered by the service, through `refuseIdentity`, which writes no line because no identity was verified to record; and the `survivors` and `restore` rows read back **`0`** users, no scratch directory and no token in any file.

**Fails when:** the `outsider` row's caller — an account that is no job account of the installation — answers `200`, or a refusal other than the two above comes back where the pairing was meant; `config.ServiceHeldSecretNames` is empty in the checkout while the job is discovered to be **keyless** (the drop landed without the code that decides it — the two moved apart, and the code is the one that decides); a `FUGARO_CREDENTIALS_SERVICE_URL` on a **shared project job** (a job the service refuses as a caller and whose provider the variable would open keyless, so its GitHub runs would mint nowhere), or the same variable on a repository job whose config in force records the repository as not switched on (the job and the record have moved apart: the runner would mint at the service while the config the launch reads says otherwise); no `FUGARO_CREDENTIALS_SERVICE_URL` on a switched-on repository's **per-repository** job (a runner with no service to ask, which is a GitHub run that halts rather than one that falls back); the bundle's policy holds a second member, a second role or a condition (Q6 broken); the unauthenticated call answers `200`, or is refused `403` **by the service** instead of by the front end — a typed refusal to a call with no identity is a call that reached the container, which is the service deployed without Cloud Run IAM, and on such a service the invoker grant is not the outer fence every row below is layered on; the mint answers anything but `200`, or names a repository that is not the calling account's, or returns a token whose reach is wider than one repository or than the run's set — a `404` on the `actions` probe is a failure with no write in it, and a `200` would mean the probe ran something; a mint is audited with a tier, or a `ghs_` string appears in any log line or in any FACT line (the check fails on its own secret scan); the pairing case is **accepted** (a job account minting for another repository, the finding review finding N1 exists to prevent), or refused with a different error type (`unverified_job_identity` where the pairing was meant, or an `unverified_run_identity` whose cause was an expired identity rather than the pairing — the two are different facts); the pairing refusal is left **unaudited** (no line for its run id: every refusal answered after `Auth.Verify` returns a whole identity is recorded, so a missing line means this refusal took `refuse`'s path instead of `refuseCall`'s and a call this service refused is unrecorded), or its line reads as something else — `purpose` `forward` where the call asked for a mint, a tier on a mint, a credential other than the App key's name, or `repository` the calling job's where the refusal is about the RUN's; or a cleanup that leaves a Firebase Auth user or a scratch file. **What failing looks like:** `func … credentialsServiceConfig` refusing where the `front-end` row is written — a deployment whose environment is incomplete, which the command refuses by name rather than guessing at (and on this tree the other shape: the service answering `state_unavailable` at the `mint` row with the bundle loader's own sentence, the operator never having run `fugaro creds set github-app-key` — a refusal at the mint's own dependency, the identity verification and the pairing having been passed); `gcloud auth print-identity-token --impersonate-service-account` refused — `iam.serviceAccounts.getOpenIdToken` is missing on the job's account, and the check stops with that name rather than widening it; a `401` from GitHub on the probes — the installation token was mistyped or the App's installation no longer covers the repository; and `signInWithCustomToken` refused — the web API key is not the sandbox Firebase project's restricted one, or the signer is not a service account of `fugaro-dev`. **What is not a failure on this release:** the job's container environment still naming `FUGARO_GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and its account still holding the accessor on it. The drop (C2.3) is held until the live result of this check proves the deployed service mints (#907), so that pair is the state this check is run against, and it is what the `app-key` row records.

**Paste back:** the one `CHECK 96 RESULT` block the script prints, from `CHECK 96 RESULT` to `CHECK 96 RESULT END (exit N)` — that is the whole of what this check asks for, and it is written so that pasting it leaks nothing: its FACT lines carry names, statuses, counts and field values, and the one shape that could carry a token is dropped and reported instead (the `secret-scan` row). Add the command line you ran and the repository you named, if you named one. **Never paste a token of any kind — no ID token, no custom token, no installation token, no access token, no web API key — and never paste a database URL in a form that carries a credential; the FACT lines above are written so that none of them needs one.** Until this check runs, the three claims of row 79 are **UNVERIFIED** live, and row 96 above stays **NOT RUN**.

**Restore.** There is nothing to roll back, and that is the point of the shape this check has: it deploys nothing, applies no Terraform, writes no database node, reads no bundle and changes no job. Three things it does change, all of them its own:

- **It can stop at the `mint` row on this tree, at the bundle**, and it says so above: the service — configured from its deployment, its account holding its own two-permission database role — admits a call's reads, so the `mint` row's call reaches the bundle, and against a bundle the operator has not filled with `fugaro creds set github-app-key` it is answered `state_unavailable` with the bundle loader's own sentence and nothing is minted. The App key's drop has not landed either (`config.ServiceHeldSecretNames` is empty, held until this check's own live result), so the job still holds the key while its runner no longer reads it — what the `app-key` row records, not a stop. The honest record of a run against an unfilled bundle is "the reads passed, the `mint` row refused at the bundle, the drop held". Nothing is left behind by a run that never got that far.
- **The Firebase Auth users its exchanges may have created** (one per run identity it exchanges, `r~<slug>~<run>`) are deleted by its last step, and the project's own user list is read back — every page of it, on a `200` — holding none of their uids. A uid is recorded **before** the exchange is attempted rather than after it answered, because the user is made *by* the exchange: an answer that was lost is a user that exists and that nothing else would name. A run that stops before that step, or whose read-back did not answer, therefore leaves the `restore` row naming the uids it may have created (with this check's own scratch run ids, `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-c96a` and `-c96b`, which is what makes them recognisable) and the one call that deletes each of them, rather than calling them gone: deleting them is the same call in the same step.
- **The one installation token it minted** (the `mint` row) cannot be un-minted and is not revoked: GitHub expires it inside the hour, and the check keeps no copy — no file, no log line, no paste-back field. If the check is run twice, the second run mints a second token, and both expire on their own. Nothing else in the installation changed, so a rerun starts from the same state.

## Check 99: the cascade end to end through the service — the probe clears a backed-off mark, a forced exhaustion walks A1 → A2 → B, a revoked token is marked broken, and a wait resumes the stage instead of spending (`fugaro-dev` only, sandbox repository only, never `belong`; run by you; NOT RUN)

**NOT RUN.** Written by Task C1.23 of [credentials-service/implementation-plan.md](credentials-service/implementation-plan.md) (its Check 99, D133, D136, D139, D140, D142, D152, D153, Global Constraints 4, 8 and 12; tasks C1.6, C1.9, C1.10, C1.11, C1.12, C1.16, C1.17, C1.19, C1.21 and C1.23); **no step of it has been run, and nothing here is a claim that it works.** It is the check of the **cascade itself**: which credential carries a call, what one account's exhaustion does to the next call, what a probe does to a backed-off mark, what a run does while it waits, and what the record and the three views say about all of it.

**⚠ What is NOT true on this tree, and why no step of this check can observe anything today.** One wired path and one missing reach, and each decides half of the evidence:

- **The service is wired end to end, holds its own database role, and is deployed for every installation — what a run reads is the per-repository switch, which no job here has on.** The installation module sets the seven names `fugaro credentials serve` reads (`FUGARO_PROJECT`, `FUGARO_GCP_PROJECT`, `FUGARO_REGION`, `FUGARO_RTDB_URL`, `FUGARO_FIREBASE_PROJECT`, `FUGARO_CREDENTIALS_SERVICE_URL`, `FUGARO_JOB_ACCOUNTS` — `deploy/terraform/gcp/modules/installation/credentials.tf`, `internal/infra/tf`'s `credentialsServiceEnv` allow-list, `internal/cli/credentials_serve.go`'s `credentialsServiceEnvNames`), the init stage fills the service's own URL as the audience, and since 0.10.1 its account holds **two** grants: the bundle's accessor (Q6) and its own custom database role `fugaroCredentialsDatabase` (`firebasedatabase.instances.get` and `.update`, on the Firebase project the database lives in), so a call's database reads are admitted — the identity verification's own read of the run's write-once outcome first among them, before the stop switches and before the bundle. What it still cannot get is a call: nothing this check does reaches it — the switch is off for every repository here (the bundle holds no model credential), so the launch hands no job the address (`FUGARO_CREDENTIALS_SERVICE_URL` is written on a per-repository job only where the switch is on, and never on a shared project job). So **no call is forwarded**: every mark this check writes by hand meets no selection, no switch is recorded, and no `waiting_until` is ever written.
- **The issuance audit line on the answer path is wired; what is queued is the served call it would describe.** `internal/credsvc/cascade.go`'s `answer` writes the issuance's own line through `auditCall`, and `refuseCall` writes one for every refusal from the identity pairing on — `audit.Write` is the write both go through — while `probe.go` and `github.go` audit the probe and the mint. So no step below may expect a **missing** line; nor may it expect a line this tree's service cannot produce: D139's **broken** mark, written by the *service* when the upstream answers 401, and the mark the 429 path writes both need a call the service actually served, and no call is served while no job is given the service's address. The run that reads them off a served call is **queued**; it adds its facts to this row, never a new check number.

So **steps 2 to 6 record `not observable`** — with the run's own halt text as the evidence rather than as a failure — and **step 1 (what is published, admitted and in force) and step 7 (nothing of the check's own survives) are what this check proves today.** What is missing — a job with the service's address, which is the release after this one — is named where it bites, and nothing in the steps' text changes when it lands. **`belong` is never touched by any step** (D147), and the sandbox repository is the only repository any step names.

**Method.** All of it is yours, at your own terminal, in one shell you keep for the check: `bash chk99.sh`, never `. chk99.sh`, so a step's `exit 1` ends the script and leaves the message where you can read it. **Four things are yours to type and export**, and the check refuses without them before it reads anything: `CHK99_OWNER_RUN=yes`, `CHK99_SANDBOX_REPO=owner/name`, and the **two admitted test accounts' names** — `CHK99_A1` and `CHK99_A2`, the account names the project's own local config carries and the bundle holds as `claude-oauth-token-<name>`. One variable is optional: `CHK99_SLUG=<repo-slug>`, for a sandbox repository with no run yet to read the slug from (step 1 prints how to read it).

**What this check writes, and who writes it.** Three things are **yours by hand**, at the database, with your own project IAM — a run token may write none of them, which is why they are hand writes and not commands: the **policy node's `credentials` member** (D153: it lives in `config/policy/shared` and nowhere else — a repository's `fugaro.yaml` cannot carry it, and `fugaro project policy publish` deliberately **preserves** whatever the node already has, so a publish neither sets nor clears it), the **marks** under `creds/marks/<name>` (only the service writes a mark as it works; `fugaro accounts clear` is the one command that writes one), and the **sandbox repository's workflow**, whose `agent.auth` must be `cascade` (its own `fugaro.yaml`, in your sandbox checkout — the check reads it out of the published policy on the launch's side, step 1). Everything else is commands: `fugaro run`, `fugaro watch`, `fugaro accounts ls`, `fugaro doctor`, `fugaro logs`, `fugaro creds set`.

**No credential value is ever typed, printed, logged, passed in an argument or written to a file by any step.** `fugaro creds set NAME` reads the value **only from stdin** — pipe it, or paste it at its hidden prompt — so the check never puts one in `argv`, in the environment or in a shell history; the revoked test token of step 4 goes in the same way, and the marks, the record and every view below carry **names** (`creds.Credential.Name`) and words (`credsvc.ValidReason`: `exhausted`, `broken`, `not_admitted`, `stopped`), never a value.

**Four runs, and each one is the check's own throwaway.** The run ids are the check's own and are **persisted in its workdir** (`$W/rid1` … `$W/rid4`), never re-derived per step: a run id is a UTC launch stamp (shape `^[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}-[0-9a-f]{4}$`), so re-deriving one mid-check would aim the check at a run that does not exist. `rid1` is the switching run (probe, A1 → A2 → B), `rid2` the revoked-token run (A2 → broken → B), `rid3` the wait under the threshold (auto), `rid4` the `oauth-only` wait. **No agent runs any step**: every launch below is a live sandbox run and every mark, the policy member and the test token are live cloud writes.

**Guard block — re-run this before every step.** The project, the region and the database host are read out of the installation's own config, never from `gcloud`'s ambient configuration, and the installation is pinned by name.

```bash
# === Check 99: setup + guard. RE-RUN THIS BLOCK BEFORE EVERY STEP. ===
I=fugaro
C=$HOME/.config/fugaro/projects/fugaro.yaml
set -u
: "${CHK99_OWNER_RUN:?type CHK99_OWNER_RUN=yes at your own terminal and export it: this check launches live sandbox runs and writes marks, a policy member and a test token}"
[ "$CHK99_OWNER_RUN" = yes ] || { echo "Check 99 stopped: CHK99_OWNER_RUN is '${CHK99_OWNER_RUN}', not 'yes'" >&2; exit 1; }
: "${CHK99_SANDBOX_REPO:?type CHK99_SANDBOX_REPO=owner/name (the sandbox repository) and export it}"
: "${CHK99_A1:?type CHK99_A1=<the name of the first admitted test account> and export it}"
: "${CHK99_A2:?type CHK99_A2=<the name of the second admitted test account> and export it}"
[ "$CHK99_A1" != "$CHK99_A2" ] || { echo "Check 99 stopped: CHK99_A1 and CHK99_A2 are both '${CHK99_A1}': this check needs two different accounts" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -r "$C" ] || { echo "Check 99 stopped: no project config at $C" >&2; exit 1; }
GCP=$(sed -n 's/^ *gcp_project: *//p' "$C" | tr -d "\"'" | head -1)
L=$(sed -n 's/^ *region: *//p' "$C" | tr -d "\"'" | head -1)
DBHOST=$(sed -n 's|^ *rtdb_url: *||p' "$C" | tr -d "\"'" | sed -e 's|^https://||' -e 's|/*$||' | head -1)
case "$GCP" in
  fugaro-dev) ;;
  *belong*|*Belong*|fugaro-prod|*prod*) echo "Check 99 stopped: '$GCP' is a belong or production project (D147)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  *) echo "Check 99 stopped: the installation's GCP project is '$GCP', not fugaro-dev" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
case "$CHK99_SANDBOX_REPO" in
  *edgeappinc*) echo "Check 99 stopped: the repository names EdgeAppInc; no step of this check may touch a production checkout" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
command -v fugaro >/dev/null && command -v gcloud >/dev/null || { echo "Check 99 stopped: fugaro or gcloud is not on PATH" >&2; exit 1; }
fugaro doctor --project "$I" --all 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^project: .*(GCP $GCP," || {
  echo "Check 99 stopped: installation '$I' is not the $GCP installation on this machine" >&2; exit 1; }
export FUGARO_PROJECT="$I"
W=/tmp/chk99; mkdir -p "$W"
[ -n "$L" ] && [ -n "$DBHOST" ] || { echo "Check 99 stopped: config carries region='$L' rtdb_url='$DBHOST'" >&2; exit 1; }
# The four credentials this check's runs choose from: two shared test accounts (tier A) and the
# sandbox project's own API key (tier B, the bundle's key anthropic-api-key).
KEY=anthropic-api-key
A1B=claude-oauth-token-$CHK99_A1      # the bundle entry the account's token is stored under
A2B=claude-oauth-token-$CHK99_A2
# The repository's slug: read from any run of it, else typed. It is the first path segment of
# the run rows (`fugaro runs ls --json` -> runs[].run = "<slug>/<run-id>").
SLUG=$(fugaro runs ls --repo "$CHK99_SANDBOX_REPO" --since 0 --json 2>/dev/null \
       | python3 -c 'import json,sys
r=json.load(sys.stdin).get("runs",[])
print(r[0]["run"].split("/")[0] if r else "")' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
[ -n "$SLUG" ] || SLUG="${CHK99_SLUG:-}"
[ -n "$SLUG" ] || { echo "Check 99 stopped: no run of $CHK99_SANDBOX_REPO to read the slug from. Read one with 'fugaro runs ls --repo $CHK99_SANDBOX_REPO --since 0', then export CHK99_SLUG=<slug>" >&2; exit 1; }
mint() { [ -s "$W/$1" ] && cat "$W/$1" || { R=$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)-$2; echo "$R" > "$W/$1"; echo "$R"; }; }
RID_CASC=$(mint rid1 99a1); RID_BROKEN=$(mint rid2 99a2); RID_WAIT=$(mint rid3 99a3); RID_OAUTH=$(mint rid4 99a4)
# The database writes this check makes are one owner token's; it is never printed and never pasted.
AT=$(gcloud auth print-access-token) || { echo "Check 99 stopped: no access token for the database" >&2; exit 1; }
db() { curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $AT" "https://${DBHOST:?}/$1"; }          # read one node
dbput() { curl -fsS -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $AT" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            --data-binary @- "https://${DBHOST:?}/$1" >/dev/null; }                    # write one node
dbdel() { curl -fsS -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $AT" "https://${DBHOST:?}/$1" >/dev/null; }
# mark NAME STATE UNTIL_SINCE... — write one mark (creds.Mark: state, until, since, backoff).
# The times are RFC 3339 UTC, relative to now in seconds (`until` -3600 is an hour ago), and
# nothing here is a credential value: a mark carries a name, a state and two instants.
mark() {
  python3 -c 'import json,sys,datetime
name,state,u,s=sys.argv[1:5]
now=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
t=lambda sec:(now+datetime.timedelta(seconds=int(sec))).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
print(json.dumps({"state":state,"until":t(u),"since":t(s)}))' "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" | dbput "creds/marks/$1.json"
}
marks() { db "creds/marks.json" | python3 -c 'import json,sys
m=json.load(sys.stdin) or {}
for k in sorted(m): print(k, m[k].get("state"), m[k].get("until",""), m[k].get("backoff",""))'
}
pol() { db "config/policy/shared/$1.json"; }   # one member of the published policy node
echo "Check 99 ready: installation=$I gcp=$GCP region=$L db=$DBHOST repo=$CHK99_SANDBOX_REPO slug=$SLUG"
echo "  accounts: A1=$CHK99_A1 ($A1B)  A2=$CHK99_A2 ($A2B)  B=$KEY"
echo "  run ids: casc=$RID_CASC broken=$RID_BROKEN wait=$RID_WAIT oauth=$RID_OAUTH"
fugaro version
```

0. **Step 0 — keep, for the Restore, the `credentials` member the policy carries now** — its exact bytes, and whether it is there at all (an absent block is a policy, not a malformed one, and it reads as the protective defaults: `oauth-only`, the 15-minute threshold, both controls at their protective values). One read, no value in it:

```bash
pol credentials | tee "$W/creds-block.before.json" | python3 -m json.tool
```
**FACT:** the block as it stands (`null` when the node carries none). **This file is the Restore's source, and nothing else in the policy node is touched by any step below.**

1. **The before-state, read-only.** *(Guard block.)* The five things every step below depends on, read before anything is written: the **switch** that makes a run use the service at all, the **credentials block** in force, the **budget the fallback spends against** (D152 refuses `fallback: auto` unless the policy enforces a per-run cap), the **two account names admitted** to the sandbox repository, and the **states** the four credentials stand in.

   ```bash
   echo "--- the policy: the switch, the block, the budget the fallback spends against ---"
   fugaro project policy show --json | python3 -c 'import json,sys
p=json.load(sys.stdin).get("policy") or {}
print("routing.claude.via:", json.dumps((p.get("routing") or {}).get("claude",{}).get("via")))
print("budget:", json.dumps(p.get("budget")))
print("credentials:", json.dumps(p.get("credentials")))
print("accounts:", json.dumps(p.get("accounts")))'
   echo "--- the repository's own admissions (config/policy/repos/<slug>) ---"
   db "config/policy/repos/$SLUG.json" | python3 -m json.tool
   echo "--- the credentials' states, and what the views say now ---"
   marks
   fugaro accounts ls --project "$I" | head -20
   fugaro doctor --project "$I" --all | grep -E '^(project|.*creds-)' | head -10
   echo "--- the sandbox workflow's agent.auth must be cascade (restore this line too) ---"
   fugaro runs ls --repo "$CHK99_SANDBOX_REPO" --since 0 | head -5
   ```
   **FACT:** `routing.claude.via` reads **`"cascade"`** and `budget.mode` **`enforce`** with `per_run_usd` **above zero** (D152: `auto` is refused on a policy that enforces no cap, and a cascade run needs the gateway). `credentials` reads `null` or a block, recorded above. `accounts.<A1>.allow_repos` and `accounts.<A2>.allow_repos` both name the sandbox repository, and the repository's own node admits both — the intersection the service computes (`credsvc.admittedAccounts`: the child's names ∩ the shared node's `allow_repos` ∩ the project's `allow_repos`). `fugaro accounts ls` prints A1 and A2 with a state, and `fugaro doctor` reports no `creds-*` finding. **If `routing.claude.via` is not `cascade`, or either account is not admitted, stop here**: nothing below can be about the cascade, and the run would carry its own credential as any other run does.
   **⚠ Not observable on this tree:** the two views at the end of the block are the *states as they stand*, which is all they can say — nothing here has been served yet.

2. **⚠ CONFIRM: the probe clears a backed-off mark, and the run is served on the account it cleared.** *(`rid1`, the switching run.)* The probe is C1.12 and it runs from the selection path: when a selection is about to answer "wait" and the credential that time belongs to is **backed off with its wait passed**, the service makes the minimal call that asks whether that credential works at all, and a success clears the mark. Two marks make that the answer, and both are needed: the tier's other account must be **unusable**, or the selection simply picks it and never consults the backed-off one.

   ```bash
   # A1: backed off, its own wait long passed, and its `since` older than D142's window
   # (the window is the policy's backoff cap, 5h by default) — so the earliest it could serve
   # work is the wait itself (`Mark.Ready` reads max(Until, Since+Window)), which is behind us,
   # and the probe is owed (`Mark.NeedsProbe`: backed off and now >= Until).
   mark "$CHK99_A1" backed_off -60 -21600        # until 1m ago, since 6h ago
   # A2: unusable, so the tier-A group has nothing the loop may take.
   mark "$CHK99_A2" exhausted 7200 -30           # until 2h from now, beyond the 15m threshold
   marks
   # ⚠ CONFIRM: the launch. A task that makes more than one call, so step 3 has a run in flight
   # to write to; keep it small and let it change nothing.
   fugaro run --repo "$CHK99_SANDBOX_REPO" --run-id "$RID_CASC" --title "check 99: the cascade" --task-file - <<'TASK'
   Do not change any file. Read the repository's README and reply with a short summary of it, then stop.
TASK

The marks are the check's own and are cleared; the runs end by themselves; the outcome nodes a launch writes are the run's own, and the runs are the check's own throwaway.

**Passes when:** the guard's ready line names `fugaro` on `fugaro-dev`, the sandbox repository, the two account names and the four run ids; step 1 shows `routing.claude.via: cascade`, an enforcing budget and both accounts admitted; step 2's run is served on the account whose backed-off mark the probe cleared; step 3's `switches` carries `exhausted` from A1 to A2 and from A2 to the paid key, with the tier-A calls notional and the tier-B calls real; step 4 shows A2 `broken` in the mark, in `fugaro accounts ls` and in `fugaro doctor`, the run moving to tier B with reason `broken`, and `available` after your clear; step 5 shows the wait, the expected resume and `resuming the stage` with `resume 1`, with nothing spent on the paid tier; step 6 shows the same marks waiting under `oauth-only` with **no** paid spend; step 7 reads every mark gone, the policy member as it was, and the `0`.

**Fails when:** a cascade run is served by a credential of its own instead of the service (step 2); a switch is taken that the switch log does not carry, or a tier-B call that the by-tier split does not count (step 3); a revoked token is retried, or a run ends because of one (step 4); a wait fails the run, or a stage is not resumed after one (step 5); a run under `oauth-only` spends on the paid tier, or is refused with a policy error while an admitted account is coming back (step 6) — **that is the D152 failure**; or a mark, the policy member or a run node is left behind (step 7).

**Paste back:** the guard's ready line, the four typed variables' **names** (never a value) and `fugaro version`; step 1's policy lines, the repository's admissions node and the `accounts ls` listing; each step's `marks` listing verbatim (names and states only — a mark holds no value); step 2's mark read-back and the run's `credential`; step 3's `switches` array and the tier lines, with the credential moves as `fugaro watch` showed them; step 4's `creds-broken` finding verbatim, A2's mark, the `clear` output and the restored `available`, **and which of the two the revoked token was** (a revoked test account's token, or a value the upstream refused); step 5's `waiting_until`, the two log lines and the run's end; step 6's `switches`, its `byTier` and the waiting line; step 7's empty `marks`, the restored policy member and the `0`. **Names, principals, states and counts — never a token, a key, an environment value or a secret's payload.** Where a step was not observable, paste the run's halt reason and detail verbatim instead.

**Restore.** The state this check leaves is the state later checks expect. Everything it writes is a throwaway, and four things must be put back:

- **The policy's `credentials` member.** Step 6's block restores it, and step 7 reads it back; if you stopped before that, put back the bytes step 0 recorded (`$W/creds-block.before.json`) — or delete the member when that read was `null`. **Do not leave `oauth-only` published**: it is the *project's* block (D153), so it is every cascade run of every repository in this project, not the sandbox's alone.
- **The marks.** Step 7 deletes the three the check writes; a step you stopped inside leaves its own — `creds/marks/<A1>`, `creds/marks/<A2>`, `creds/marks/anthropic-api-key` — and **do not leave a mark standing**: an exhausted mark holds a credential out of service until its reset, and a broken one until a person clears it.
- **The test account's token.** Step 4 puts the real one back with `fugaro creds set "$A2B"`; if you stopped inside it, do that by hand at your own terminal. The bundle holds the value, never this check.
- **The sandbox workflow's `agent.auth`.** It was `cascade` before the check (step 1 read it) and it stays `cascade`; if you changed it to run a step, change it back — a `cascade` workflow whose project has no credentials block is refused at launch (the gateway is what carries its calls), and one left on `cascade` after you turn the block off is a repository whose runs halt.
- **Nothing else.** No rule, no secret version, no service, no IAM: this check reads the bundle's *names* (`fugaro creds ls`), never a value, and never opens the container. The four runs are throwaway and their own records age out with the runs bucket's lifecycle.

## Check 100: the QR pairing, and what the code proves (installation `fugaro`, never `belong`, project `fugaro-dev`, with your own phone; run by you; NOT RUN)

**NOT RUN.** Task P6.11 writes this check and running it is the owner's; its subject is the functional spec's §4.1 pairing, the reconciliation's **U5** (*a custom token's `exp` below an hour is honoured by `signInWithCustomToken`*) and the owner's amendment of 2026-10-20. It is written now and run after the release that carries `fugaro pair` — a check is never run before its text is in the register — and **the guard stops today**: neither `fugaro pair` (`internal/cli/pair.go`, P6.6) nor the app's pairing screen (`mobile/src/pairing/`, P6.8) is built, so nothing can mint a pairing token and no phone can scan one.

**Pairing is discovery, not identity, and this check is written to that rule.** The code tells the phone **which project and which orchestrator endpoint** to connect to, and **grants no access by itself**: the pairing token is a short-lived custom token admitted only to write its **own** request node (the `PAIRING` macro — `auth.token.pu != null && auth.token.pu == auth.uid` on a `p~` uid, `internal/budget/rules/rules.go`), and a `p~` session reads and writes no project node it does not own.
